Headline: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Pickens is still stuck in the questionable column, though his continued participation is a good sign. The team allowed him to play through the injury in Week 8 against the Cardinals, which was probably the wrong call. He sat out last week despite practicing in a limited capacity. Hopefully, he upgrades to full participation tomorrow. Stay tuned.

Headline: Joey Porter (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Porter reportedly told reporters that his “whole foot is jacked up.” That sounds bad. He was able to run today, and hadn’t in a while, but declined to say whether he will play in Week 10 against the 49ers. We suspect he will sit out this weekend’s contest.

Headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Harrison was limited yesterday and sat out today. That series of events typically suggests that the player was injured in practice. Harrison is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this time. He can be stashed in 12-team leagues, but it may take him a while to get back into form.

Headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
News Snippet: Dell is firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Browns. He led the team with nine targets last week, catching four passes for 105 yards and one touchdown. The coaching staff reportedly drew up a play just to get him over the century mark. He is a FLEX starter this week.

Headline: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: This morning, Boston told reporters that he was hoping to resume practicing today. Unfortunately, he was unable to do so. That said, Boston’s toe injury is feeling better and things are “trending up” at the moment. It sounds like the rookie wide receiver has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Texans and would be a WR3/FLEX if so.

Headline: Micah Parsons (knee/illness) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Parsons seemingly has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Vikings, but he remains in the questionable column at this time. Packers DC Jonathan Gannon has done well with Parsons sidelined. Getting him back will only improve the unit.

Headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
News Snippet: We got word early on Wednesday that Worthy would suit up for practice. He ended up being a full participant and remained full today, putting him firmly on track to play in Week 10 against the Falcons. Worthy is down to being a touchdown-dependent FLEX with Josh Downs now on the roster, but his presence helps out Patrick Mahomes.

Headline: Chris Bell (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Dolphins were regularly limiting Bell’s practice reps earlier this season, so this may just be routine maintenance. The rookie wide receiver was limited yesterday. Bell has not yet established himself as a fantasy-relevant player, and he is unlikely to do so in Kyle McCord’s first start, especially if his surgically repaired knee is bothering him.

Headline: Trent McDuffie (back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
News Snippet: Yesterday, The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reported that the Rams were hopeful that McDuffie would play in Week 10 against the Cardinals. He is tentatively on track to do so with today’s return to practice. The Rams will potentially morph into a run-heavy team that relies on the defense to generate turnovers with their top-two wide receivers and top tight end sidelined. McDuffie can help them accomplish that.

Headline: Taliese Fuaga (knee) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Saints’ right tackle was added to the injury report today, which is extremely unfortunate. The team is already without center Erik McCoy (biceps). Hopefully, this is only a minor issue for Fuaga.

Headline: Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: Back-to-back limited sessions have us believing Cooper has a good chance to play in Week 10 against the Bills. The role has been up-and-down as the Jets struggle to work in all their weapons. Cooper qualifies as a FLEX play against what has been a shaky Bills defense when not facing Carson Wentz this season.

Headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Etienne is firmly in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 10 game against the Panthers. New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill believes that the Saints would keep Etienne on a snap count if he makes his return this weekend, noting “they took it easy” on Jordyn Tyson, who returned from a lengthy hamstring injury last week. If active, Etienne likely warrants low-end RB2 treatment.

Headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: Wilson still needs to be officially cleared from concussion protocol to play, but two limited sessions have him with a real chance to be active in Week 10 after missing Week 9. If he can play, Wilson will likely be an upside fantasy WR2 against the Bills.

Headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
News Snippet: Meyers was limited at today’s practice. He is on track to play through the injury this week after doing so successfully last week, along with a hamstring injury. The Jaguars’ dominance has rendered Meyers somewhat of a touchdown-reliant FLEX starter, though this is a soft matchup against the Titans.

Headline: Dalton Kincaid (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: After two limited sessions we don’t have a lot of doubt that Kincaid will be ready to play in Week 10’s game against the Jets. He may be managed a bit, though, as he toughs it out. He’ll remain a TE1 play regardless.

Headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Rodriguez played through the hand injury without issue last week, totaling 10 carries and two receptions on Thursday night. He should again handle a FLEX-worthy workload against the Titans in Week 10, with Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) managing something.

Headline: Jared Goff (chest) practiced in full on Thursday.
News Snippet: That should alleviate any concern that he’d miss Sunday morning’s Munich kickoff against the Patriots. Goff will be a low-end QB1 for that one assuming no major negative news hits on Friday.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Tuten sat out all three practices before playing in last week’s Thursday Night Football game, totaling 12 carries in the process. We tentatively expect him to play in Week 10 against the Titans, and he should be in fantasy football lineups even if he sits out or is limited on Friday. Stay tuned.

Headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: He played through this last week, managing an 8/86 line against the Dolphins. We’d be surprised if he wasn’t removed from the injury report tomorrow after getting in two limited sessions on Wednesday and Thursday.

Headline: Cade Mays (ankle) will not play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
News Snippet: He did not travel to Munich with the team and has not practiced since injuring his ankle in Week 8. Juice Scruggs will continue to fill in at center.

Headline: D.J. Reed (hip) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
News Snippet: Reed has not practiced since injuring his hip in Week 8. The Lions’ secondary remains a patchwork effort against Drake Maye and the Patriots.

Headline: Kerby Joseph (knee) won’t play in Detroit’s Week 10 game against the Patriots.
News Snippet: Joseph got in a full practice session with the Lions on Thursday, but will not travel to Munich with the club. It sounds like he’ll have a real chance to play in Week 11 when the Lions head back to the states.

Headline: Peter Skoronski (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Titans’ starting left guard is very unlikely to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars, who field a top-tier defense. Skoronski has been sidelined since injuring his hamstring in Week 8 against the Bengals.

Headline: Tony Pollard (finger/rest) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Pollard practiced in full yesterday, despite the finger injury. The Titans added the rest label to his listing today, indicating his absence is simply load management. We do not expect his snaps to be impacted by the finger injury this weekend. Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing, though, which could hurt Pollard’s snap share. Stay tuned.

Headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: He played off a questionable tag last week with a more checked practice report, so we’d be surprised if Henry didn’t go on Sunday. He has a real chance of being cleared off the injury report altogether on Friday after a pair of limited sessions to open the week.

Headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. Post-Week 9 reports had Stevenson with a chance to miss a short period of time, but a limited session at least points to the idea that he could play in Munich on Sunday morning. Fantasy managers reliant on Stevenson or dabbling with Corey Kiner will want to keep an eye on Friday’s injury report.

Headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
News Snippet: Spears was listed as a limited participant on today’s injury report, theoretically giving him a chance to play in Week 10 against the Jaguars’ elite run defense. Spears’ potential return could lower Tony Pollard’s snap share a tad, though Spears does not need to be rostered in 10-team leagues.

Headline: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: Two limited practices would seem to have him with a real chance to play in Munich, and the fact that he made the trip at all makes it seem likely he’ll have a real chance to go. We’d consider him on the optimistic side of questionable heading into Friday’s practice report.

Headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
News Snippet: The Saints’ veteran running back is just having his reps managed. With Audric Estime playing well and Travis Etienne (hamstring) potentially returning, Kamara does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time. Kamara will continue to chip in on passing downs, though. Backup RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder) remains sidelined.

Headline: James Pearce Jr. (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP for the 23-year-old. Pearce Jr. will probably at least hit the questionable line on Friday and has a chance to be cleared off altogether if things trend in the right direction. Kevin Stefanski did not seem overly concerned about his status when asked about it, saying the Falcons “also want him to get healthy and feel good.”

Headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: He was instantly ruled out ahead of Atlanta’s date in Madrid last Monday and has not practiced since. With the bye on tap in Week 11, we’d expect Branch to sit against the Chiefs.

Headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
News Snippet: Phillips practiced in full yesterday. Today, he was only limited. Hm. Today’s lightened workload could be a planned load management decision, but tomorrow’s practice participation will be worth watching for the Panthers’ top pass rusher. The Panthers’ stud LG Damien Lewis (knee) was also downgraded today, while starting perimeter CB Mike Jackson (groin) remained a full participant.

Headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) worked out with trainers on the side during Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: He did not elevate beyond an official DNP today, but this is an actual step after Tate missed four consecutive practices and Week 8 sandwiched around their Week 9 bye. He’ll have a non-zero chance to play this week heading into Friday, but you have to imagine the best we’ll see on Friday is a questionable tag.

Headline: Woody Marks (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Per Aaron Wilson, he injured the knee in Wednesday’s practice and was experiencing discomfort. We don’t necessarily think Marks is in major trouble yet considering “discomfort” isn’t exactly a major injury, and he has been remarkably durable in game. But there is certainly a chance he’ll miss Week 10’s game against the Browns and fantasy managers should be prepared to pivot on Friday.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said to “expect a lot of Cam Skattebo” in Week 10 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: The Giants host the Commanders for this week’s Thursday Night Football game. The open-air stadium is currently experiencing heavy rain, and Fowler indicates the rainfall will continue this evening. Devin Singletary will back up Skattebo, but the touch distribution will heavily “slant” toward Skattebo, solidifying his status as an RB2.

Headline: David Montgomery (groin) returned to practice on Thursday.
News Snippet: Montgomery was mostly working out with a trainer, but DeMeco Ryans said they were “pleased with the progress he was making.” It’s possible this goes down as a DNP still on the official report, but it is real progress that he’s back on the field and he now has a non-zero chance to suit up for Week 10.

Headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur indicated that Luke Musgrave (neck) “probably” will not play in 2026.
News Snippet: Earlier this season, the Packers thought that Musgrave had a chance to return. Unfortunately, it appears as though that is no longer the case. The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Musgrave’s “tenure with the Packers is all but over.”

Headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes the Packers should not sign MarShawn Lloyd to an extension after next season.
News Snippet: Schneidman believes it is “not possible” to sign Lloyd to an extension after the 2027 season because of the young running back’s poor play. Lloyd is still trying to beat defenders around the edge with speed, rather than running north-south when he needs to. Although the injuries are mostly behind him, he has failed to live up to preseason expectations. Lloyd does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats at this time.

Headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports the 49ers and Chiefs “were interested” in Garrett Wilson ahead of the trade deadline.
News Snippet: The Jets made it clear they were not moving Wilson early in the process, so we can’t imagine trade talks between them and either team made it very far. Cimini notes that the Jets could revisit a Wilson trade in the offseason. Wilson told reporters earlier this year that he loves it in New York, but he loves winning more. The Jets haven’t done much of that since Wilson was drafted. This will be a storyline to watch in the offseason, though we suspect he’ll remain in New York for the forseeable future.

Headline: Former Bucs head coach Bruce Arians says he has “the itch” to coach football again.
News Snippet: Arians detailed myriad health issues that he dealt with in his final season as the Bucs’ head coach. He tore his Achilles and eventually injured his back. Arians was also monitoring an aneurysm in his heart at the time. He stepped away from coaching after the 2021 season but remained with the Bucs in an advisory role for some time. Arians won 13 games in his final season as a head coach and took home the Lombardi Trophy in his penultimate season. Now 74 years old, Arians wouldn’t be the long-term answer for a team, but he could be an option for a team in a win-now window. He later stated that he would consider returning to the Bucs and is only interested in a head-coaching role.

Headline: Bengals designated Andrei Iosivas (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Iosivas will practice today for the first time since injuring his thumb in Week 2. The Bengals have 21 days to officially activate him from injured reserve, though he practiced in full today. He will likely reclaim his No. 3 role once healthy, though we don’t expect much fantasy value to come of it.

Headline: Ravens signed K Harrison Mevis to their practice squad.
News Snippet: The team added Riley Patterson to their active roster yesterday, but both kickers will likely have a chance to earn the job in practice this week. We aren’t expecting great fantasy numbers from either kicker with Lamar Jackson no longer fueling the offense.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Broncos have revoked their trade for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley because of a failed physical.
News Snippet: The move, or lack thereof, was announced by Denver around midnight, and Rapoport later gave the reasoning. Henley has been playing through a knee issue for multiple weeks, though he has also dealt with other injuries that could have caused the Broncos to back out. Denver originally agreed to give fourth- and fifth-round picks to acquire Henley. He will now return to the Chargers. As Rapoport points out, the 0-8 Chargers now officially made zero trades ahead of the deadline.

Headline: Deommodore Lenoir (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Lenoir and Renardo Green (back) were among the two 49ers cornerbacks not practicing on Wednesday. Fellow cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder/neck) was a limited participant. With the slew of secondary injuries, the Cowboys wideouts will have an easier chance at chunk gains against San Francisco for Week 10.

Headline: Leonard Williams (stinger) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Williams missed last week due to a stinger and continues to be sidelined. He will need to practice in some fashion to have a chance at playing in Week 10 against the Raiders.

Headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Shaheed has missed the last two weeks with a knee injury, but he was able to practice in full to open Week 10. A full practice participation is a good sign we’ll see Shaheed on the field for Week 10 against the Raiders. He has been splitting WR2 opportunities with Cooper Kupp this year and belongs on fantasy benches until further notice.

Headline: Charles Cross (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Cross remains sidelined with a high ankle sprain he suffered in Week 7. He is yet to return to practice and therefore is trending towards missing Week 10 against the Raiders; a full practice participation would be needed to feel confident about his chances of playing this week.

Headline: Travon Walker (rib) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Walker suffered a rib injury in practice last week but played through it in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens. He starts out the week not practicing, but this may just be maintenance instead of an aggravation. Walker will need to practice in some fashion later this week, but he is not in jeopardy of missing Week 10 against the Titans just yet.

Headline: Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Rodriguez was limited last week and played through the hand injury in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens. He was limited again to open Week 10 but is still trending to play against the Titans. With Bhayshul Tuten still dealing with ankle and foot injuries, Rodriguez is a good bet to split touches this week and achieve FLEX value against a weak Titans defense.

Headline: Jakobi Meyers (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week, but played through them in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens. It is discouraging that he did not practice after a mini-bye, but the good news is that he only has the ankle designation now, no hamstring. Meyers is not yet in jeopardy of missing Week 10, but will need to practice in some fashion for fantasy managers to feel confident about his chances of playing against the Titans.

Headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Tuten was listed as DNP with the same ankle/foot injuries he played through last Thursday. He was clearly limited in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens and it is a bit discouraging that he starts out Week 10 not practicing after a mini-bye. It’s still early in the week, so this may just be injury maintenance for the 23-year-old. A practice later in the week will ease fantasy managers’ concerns, but a split in touches with Chris Rodriguez is certainly on the table again for Week 10 against the Titans.

Headline: Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Froholdt is the Cardinals’ starting center and is trending to miss Week 10 against the Rams as he deals with a concussion. Backup interior offensive lineman Jon Gaines (ankle) also missed practice, leaving the Cardinals’ offensive line depleted with a matchup against Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald coming up this week.

Headline: Dion Dawkins (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Dawkins did not practice last week due to a rib injury, missing the Bills’ Week 9 win over the Vikings. he returns to practice in a limited fashion to open Week 10, giving him a chance to return against the Jets.

Headline: Myles Garrett (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s walk-through.
News Snippet: Garrett returned from injured reserve and played in Week 9 against the Commanders. A limited listing indicates the 30-year-old will be managing his practice reps as he ramps back up from the knee injury. Expect Garrett to play in Week 10 against the Cardinals.

Headline: Steve Avila (hamstring) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
News Snippet: Avila aggravated a hamstring injury and starts out the week not practicing. Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Avila will miss some time, but may not go on injured reserve as the Rams are out of return slots. Expect Avila to miss Week 10 against the Cardinals.

Headline: Kam Curl (toe) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
News Snippet: Curl played through a foot injury in Week 9 but picked up a toe injury. He starts out the week not practicing but will have a chance to play Week 10 against the Cardinals if he can get a practice in later this week.

Headline: Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) did not practice in Wednesday’s walk-through.
News Snippet: Ferguson was listed as a DNP for the Rams’ Wednesday walk-through. Rams head coach Sean McVay said earlier this week that Ferguson is likely out a couple week, so this comes as no surprise. Meanwhile, fellow tight ends Davis Allen (oblique) and Colby Parkinson (ribs) were both listed as limited participants. Allen and Parkinson are trending towards playing in Week 10 against the Cardinals, with Parkinson operating more as a pass-catcher and Allen as a blocker.

Headline: Marshawn Lloyd (knee) was not listed on the Packers’ Wednesday injury report.
News Snippet: Lloyd was presumably a full go in practice on Wednesday as he did not appear on the Packers’ injury report at all to open Week 10. This indicates he will be ready to play this week against the Vikings, despite missing Week 9 due to a knee injury. With Josh Jacobs out, Lloyd will see backfield opportunities once again. Kaleb Johnson projects to get a shot at the lead back role initially, but Lloyd has a passing-down role in the backfield. In the midst of an inefficient season and facing a daunting Vikings defense, Lloyd is a shaky FLEX at best for fantasy teams in Week 10.

Headline: Ravens signed K Riley Patterson, formerly of the Dolphins.
News Snippet: The Ravens currently have Tyler Loop on injured reserve and lost Jake Moody to the Falcons this week. This prompted a couple of kicker workouts this week and led to the team signing Patterson to be the kicker, at least until Loop returns. Patterson made 27-of-29 field goals for the Dolphins last season and 7-of-9 field goals this season. Miami released him in October and he finds a new home in Baltimore a few weeks later. Patterson will kick for the Ravens on Monday Night Football against the Chargers, but doesn’t have much fantasy value with a Ravens offense missing Lamar Jackson.

Headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) worked out with trainers on the side during Thursday’s practice.
News Snippet: He may not elevate beyond an official DNP today, but this is an actual step after Tate missed four consecutive practices and Week 8 sandwiched around their Week 9 bye. He’ll have a non-zero chance to play this week heading into Friday, but you have to imagine the best we’ll see on Friday is a questionable tag.

Headline: Bengals designated Andrei Iosivas (thumb) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Iosivas will practice today for the first time since injuring his thumb in Week 2. The Bengals have 21 days to officially activate him from injured reserve. He will likely reclaim his No. 3 role once healthy, though we don’t expect much fantasy value to come of it.

Headline: Ben Brown (knee) will not play in Week 10 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Brown recently moved to left guard to fill that hole in the Pats’ lineup. He’s now out for Week 10 and Walter Rouse, his backup, is in the league’s concussion protocol. New England could be severely undermanned in the trenches for their matchup versus Detroit.

Headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Stevenson is expected to miss some time because of the knee issue. With their bye next week, it makes sense for the Pats to hold him out on Sunday and give him an extra week of rest. With TreVeyon Henderson already ruled out, Corey Kiner is the next man up in this backfield. As the only game in town for touches, he will push for an RB2 ranking this week.

Headline: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) will not play in Week 10 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Henderson is dealing with an unexpected medical emergency right now. We would imagine he did not travel to Germany with the team. It’s unclear when he will return. With Rhamondre Stevenson also expected to miss Week 10, Corey Kiner is in line to see the bulk of the team’s backfield touches this week.

Headline: A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Brown traveled to Germany with the team and is already practicing to start the week, giving him a shot at suiting up on Sunday morning. Given his lengthy history of knee issues, it still wouldn’t surprise us if he gets another week off. Brown would be in line for a strong workload and WR2 fantasy numbers if active. Fantasy managers will want to monitor this situation throughout the week.

Headline: Marvin Harrison (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Harrison is tentatively on track to play in Week 10 against the Browns, but hamstring strains can be tough for wide receivers to immediately bounce back from, and we do not know whether the injury occurred today or last Sunday. Harrison’s practice participation tomorrow will tell us more. Stay tuned.

Headline: Woody Marks (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Marks should be good to go for the Texans’ Week 10 game against the Browns, though this backfield is awfully banged up. Marks totaled 18 carries and four targets last week, and should again handle a sizable workload this week. Unfortunately, he has not proven to be an efficient player and may need to score a touchdown to return RB2 value.

Headline: Tank Dell (hand/shoulder) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: The Texans’ diminutive wide receiver led the team with nine targets last week, and evidently got a little banged up in the process. Dell’s early-week participation puts him on track to face the Browns this weekend though. He is a FLEX starter, assuming he is good to go.

Headline: Denzel Boston (toe) did not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Boston continues to pick up lower-leg injuries, but last week’s calf issue did not slow him down. The Browns have begun varying Boston’s usage, no longer limiting him to high-variance downfield work. Adding short-to-intermediate opportunities only enhances his outlook. If he can play this weekend, he will be a WR3/FLEX.

Headline: James Pearce Jr. (back) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: The former No. 26 overall pick made his season debut last week. A back injury flared up on him headed into the week, but he ultimately pushed through it on Sunday. It’s unclear if the team is just managing his reps with the DNP today or if the issue got worse. Tomorrow’s injury report will be more revealing.

Headline: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Branch suffered the hamstring injury in Week 8 and missed last week’s game because of it. He appears to be on pace to miss another game. With just 10 catches to his name after nearly as many weeks, 2026 is shaping up to be an underwhelming start to Branch’s career.

Headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Jordyn Tyson should get “a healthy dose more” snaps in Week 10 against the Panthers.
News Snippet: Moore adds that the Saints will continue to increase Tyson’s usage over time, “to a point where he’s not limited.” This is great to read. Tyson isn’t even listed on the Saints’ injury report this week. He earned four targets on 16 snaps last week and should be expected to increase his workload this week, potentially to a FLEX-worthy level.

Headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) did not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: On the plus side, Donaldson is no longer listed with a concussion. Audric Estime played well last week and Travis Etienne (hamstring) is practicing now, though. Donaldson could be phased out.

Headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: The Chiefs have been limiting Kelce’s participation on Wednesdays in recent weeks. His return to full participation to begin the week is great to see. Kelce, 37, remains a locked-in TE1 at this point in his career. Treat him accordingly against the Falcons.

Headline: Rashee Rice (knee) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: For the first time since October 4th, the Chiefs listed Rice only with a knee issue. He had been managing a hamstring strain for more than a month, prior to today, and was typically limited early in the week. This is a great sign for his health moving forward. Rice is a WR2 against the Falcons.

Headline: Justin Fields (neck) is practicing in full in Week 10 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: Fields may have picked up a neck injury while attempting a Tush Push last week. Backup quarterback injuries are not always relevant, but with Patrick Mahomes (elbow) nursing a small injury, this is notable.

Headline: Jaylen Wright (quad) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Colts.
News Snippet: Wright missed last week with the quad issue. Kaytron Allen played through a quad issue of his own, though he only saw one carry. Allen practiced in full today as well. Wright will return to a distant RB2 role for Week 10. He is not on the fantasy radar right now.

Headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that Trent McDuffie (back) will not practice on Wednesday, but the Rams are hopeful he will play in Week 10 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: Groin and back injuries have plagued McDuffie for some time, but it sounds like he has a chance to face the division-rival Cardinals in Week 10. With the Rams’ receiving corps ailing, Los Angeles could turn into an old-school team, featuring a high-volume run game and a lockdown defense.

Headline: T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Both injuries are new for the veteran tight end. He presumably suffered them in the Vikings’ Monday loss to the Bills, though it’s unclear exactly when in the game he got hurt. Gavin Bartholomew would be the next man up, though we doubt he’s the best option off the waiver wire in most fantasy leagues.

Headline: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
News Snippet: We expect to see Kamara listed with his typical NIR-rest/back designation when the team’s official injury report is released later today. An update will be provided if this is not the case. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) now practicing and Audric Estime playing well, Kamara is barely fantasy-relevant.

Headline: Travis Etienne (hamstring) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Coming off injured reserve, Etienne can practice for 21 days before the Saints must officially either activate him or shut him down. The Saints’ No. 1 running back has been sidelined since unsuccessfully trying to play through a hamstring strain in Week 3 against the Raiders. Audric Estime could warrant RB2/FLEX treatment again this week if Etienne is not ready to face the Panthers on Sunday.

Headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Skattebo was listed as doubtful for Week 9. He reportedly pushed to play, but the team smartly chose to hold him out. He logged two full practices this week and is good to go for Thursday’s game. Without much competition for touches, Skattebo is back in the RB2 mix.

Headline: Cade Mays (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: The Lions are at their best when the offensive line is in good health. Mays missed multiple games early in the year with a wrist injury. He is now sidelined by an ankle injury. Hopefully, he can resume practicing before long. Lions S Kerby Joseph (knee) and S Brian Branch (hip) were both limited.

Headline: J.J. McCarthy (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Commanders.
News Snippet: McCarthy was upgraded to a full practice yesterday and remained full today. He’s good to go after getting banged up in the team’s Week 9 win over the Eagles. McCarthy made a few big plays against Philly, but his accuracy issues were compounded by five sacks. His shine as a high-end QB2 has all but evaporated.

Headline: Sione Vaki (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Vaki played through the injury last week, and should be expected to do so again against the Patriots this week. Fellow backup RB Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring) is practicing in full. Vaki is the team’s top backup.

Headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: St. Brown played through the injury without issue last week, catching eight passes for 86 yards. The Lions’ No. 1 wide receiver should be treated as a WR1, as usual, against the Patriots in this week’s international game. St. Brown will likely upgrade to full participation on Thursday or Friday.

Headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Turpin has missed three weeks with the rib issue. He may need to be upgraded to a full practice before being cleared to return to action. Even if he is back this week, George Pickens appears to be healthy and Ryan Flournoy is locked in as the team’s WR3, so there isn’t any fantasy value to be had here.

Headline: Dalton Kincaid (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Kincaid has successfully played through a couple of injuries this season, and we expect that to be the case again this week, when the Bills face the Jets. Kincaid’s early-week limited participation puts him on track to play. He is a TE1 in this divisional showdown.

Headline: Hunter Henry (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
News Snippet: Henry played through the foot issue last week despite a severely limited practice regimen throughout the week. He only caught three passes for 35 yards, though the Pats failed to get much going on offense while the game was competitive. He should rebound as a high-end TE2 for his Week 10 date with the Lions.

Headline: Carlton Davis (knee) will not play in Week 10 against the Lions.
News Snippet: The Pats are traveling to Germany to take on the Lions. Davis was among several players who presumably didn’t make the trip overseas and were ruled out today. Davis has two pass breakups and 22 combined tackles across five appearances this season.

Headline: Bam Knight (concussion) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Knight sat out in Week 9 against the Seahawks, but he is on track to resume his lead rushing role against the Rams this week. He was seen wearing a yellow non-contact jersey today, and will likely be listed as limited. The Rams’ defense is enjoying improved health and playing well. Knight will likely handle a FLEX-worthy role, but producing a ceiling game against this defense may be unlikely.

Headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Murray is expected to miss more time with the Grade Two hamstring injury. With Kirk Cousins back in Minnesota, Murray’s health doesn’t change much for the offense. He will likely serve as Cousins’ backup once he gets past the hamstring issue.

Headline: Jauan Jennings (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Jennings missed Week 9 against the Bills with the calf issue and looks likely to sit for at least one more game. Myles Price ran ahead of Tai Felton last week, putting him in line for another round of No. 3 duties in Week 10. He is not on the fantasy radar despite the uptick in snaps.

Headline: Jared Goff (chest) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Goff had his worst game of the year in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins. Perhaps this injury was bothering him. On the plus side, Goff is already practicing in a limited capacity, so we do not expect it to impact his availability for Week 10 against the Patriots. It is worth monitoring his practice participation level this week, though.

Headline: Jake Ferguson (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: No surprises here as Ferguson is expected to miss multiple weeks, according to Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Ferguson was barely putting up TE2 numbers when healthy, so we’re not expecting much from Brevyn Spann-Ford as the next man up. Fantasy managers should aim higher on the waiver wire this week.

Headline: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Porter Jr. was on the practice field with his helmet on, but he ultimately watched as the rest of the defense went through the session. He was playing through the ankle issue for a while before missing Week 9 against Arizona. A DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 10, but things could change if he manages a limited session on Thursday.

Headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Okonkwo is one of many fringe TE1/2 candidates on any given week. He does not need to be in fantasy football lineups, but he can act as a serviceable fill-in, though his upside is most touchdown-dependent.

Headline: Peter Skoronski (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: A DNP after the bye puts Skoronski on the wrong side of questionable to start the week. Skoronski went down with the hamstring issue during the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals. Garrett Dellinger took his spot in the lineup then and could be in line for his first career start this week.

Headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Spears’ lingering knee issue appeared to get worse a few weeks ago when the team scratched him for Week 7. He was held out the following week and even their recent bye doesn’t seem to have done the trick. Tony Pollard will continue to see a glut of touches until Spears gets healthy.

Headline: Treylon Burks (foot) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 10 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Burks got in a limited session on Tuesday, but was held out of practice on Monday and Wednesday. It is entirely possible that the Commanders are just exercising caution and Burks will play his normal allotment of snaps, but this sure seems like a scenario where he could end up being a decoy. Burks should be viewed as a boom-bust FLEX with a very low floor.

Headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jalen Travis (knee) is expected to miss 2-4 weeks.
News Snippet: A fourth-round pick in 2025, Travis made four starts as a rookie and took over as the team’s starting right tackle this year. He started all nine games to open the season. Luke Tenuta will take his place in the lineup for a few weeks.

Headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that the Rams are “hopeful” that Davante Adams (hamstring) will return for Week 13 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: Over the next three weeks, the Rams face the Cardinals, go on bye and then face the Packers. While his potential return ahead of the fantasy football playoffs is helpful, we still have a long way to go before he returns, and even then, his status for Week 13 is still uncertain. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and CJ Daniels appear to be in line for 11 personnel duties at this time.

Headline: Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not be placed on injured reserve for roster mechanics reasons.
News Snippet: The Rams are running out of return from IR designations. Putting Nacua on injured reserve would prevent another player from coming back later in the season, so he will simply take up a 53-man roster spot while he recovers. McVay made it clear that Nacua will still be out for a while. Nacua is expected to return at some point this year, though whether or not the Rams are still in the playoff hunt once he’s healthy could factor into the timeline.

Headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not practice on Wednesday.
News Snippet: The 49ers are smartly allowing Evans to fully recover from his Achilles tendinitis rather than allowing him to try to play through it. On Sunday, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that Evans was “questionable at best” for Week 10 against the Cowboys. He should probably be considered doubtful to play at this time.

Headline: Carson Beck will start for the Cardinals in Week 10 against the Rams.
News Snippet: With Jacoby Brissett in Baltimore and Gardner Minshew out because of a UCL injury, the Cardinals are already down to their third-string quarterback. It was almost a given that Beck would start at some point this year, though we imagine head coach Matt LaFleur didn’t think it would be this soon. Beck played well in his lone preseason appearance, throwing for 188 yards and a score. While he’s not much of a streaming option this week, he should be good enough to keep Trey McBride at the top of the TE1 ranks, especially with Michael Wilson done for the year.

Headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will resume practicing in a limited capacity on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Samuel now has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys’ fantasy-friendly defense. The 49ers could play things cautiously and give him more time off, but an early-week return is usually a good sign. With much of the 49ers’ pass-catching corps still banged up, Samuel could return to a WR3/flex-worthy workload right away. He should be added wherever he is available. Samuel later told reporters that he feels “ready” to play on game day.

Headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quentin Nelson (knee) could play in Week 12 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: Macdonald also said that Nelson is “back” with the team this week. It’s unclear whether he means Nelson has simply returned to the facility to participate in team meetings, or if he actually has a chance to practice, though we assume Nelson will not practice until after the Seahawks’ Week 11 bye. Nelson underwent a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee last week. If he indeed returns in Week 12, the surgery will have only cost him two games. Stay tuned.

Headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Michael Wilson’s prognosis is “really good for the future.”
News Snippet: Wilson suffered a fracture in his neck on the fourth play of Week 9. He somehow finished the game but was placed on season-ending injured reserve after testing revealed the full extent of the injury. The good news is that this doesn’t sound like it will change the outlook of his career. He will be back next season as the Cardinals’ top wideout unless they make a big splash at his position in the offseason.

Headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock (elbow/oblique) will not “take every rep and throw” during Week 10 practices.
News Snippet: Lock was a limited practice participant through Week 9 practices before starting on game day. We expect that to be the case again this week. Fellow backup QB Jalen Milroe will take some first-team reps to help preserve Lock for the Seahawks’ Week 10 game against the Raiders. Given the injuries, Lock is likely just a mid-to-low QB2 despite the soft matchup.

Headline: Steelers did not open Michael Pittman’s (foot) 21-day practice window.
News Snippet: This is unfortunate, but it likely benefits Germie Bernard in the short term. Pittman told reporters that he had hoped to return following the Steelers’ Week 9 bye. The team will likely choose to ramp him up for at least one week once they open his 21-day practice window. Doing so tomorrow or Friday seems unlikely.

Headline: Steelers opened Derrick Harmon’s (foot) 21-day practice window.
News Snippet: The Steelers’ talented interior defender reportedly has a chance to play in Week 10 against the Bengals. Harmon suffered his foot injury early in Week 4 against the Browns. This season, has totaled 12 tackles, one TFL, 1.5 NFL sacks and a forced fumble. Getting him back will be a plus for the Steelers’ defense.

Headline: Carson Wentz (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: The Vikings conducted a walkthrough today, so this is just an estimate. Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said he is “hopeful” that Wentz will be available for backup duties in Week 10 against the Packers, though Max Brosmer is a possibility.

Headline: Panthers designated Jonathon Brooks (core) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Brooks practiced in full, giving him a shot at suiting up this week. However, it won’t surprise us if they give him another week of practice before putting him back on the field because of his lengthy injury history. With Chuba Hubbard excelling in his workhorse role this year, Brooks will likely be stuck with change-of-pace duties once healthy. He is only worth stashing in deeper fantasy formats.

Headline: Panthers designated Xavier Leggette (knee) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Legette practiced in full, so he could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. He would only return to a part-time role, so there isn’t any fantasy value to be had here. Jonathon Brooks is also practicing, meaning the Panthers’ offense could be getting reinforcements at multiple positions soon.

Headline: Patriots designated Reggie Gilliam (knee) to return from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Gilliam’s return allows the Patriots to increase their 21 and 22 personnel usage. This in turn should help out the Patriots’ run game, while also reducing target competition for the established skill position players. Gilliam is not fantasy-relevant on his own, though.

Headline: David Montgomery (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: It looks like Montgomery will miss another game because of the groin issue. Woody Marks has been seeing all the work in his absence. The role has yet to produce a meaningful fantasy outing. Still, fantasy managers can’t afford to fade a player seeing the bulk of the touches in an ascending offense. Marks remains a frustrating RB2 for Week 10.

Headline: Vikings GM Nolan Teasley said there is “always potential” for Kirk Cousins to remain in Minnesota beyond 2026, but acquiring him was about this season.
News Snippet: It seems that the Vikings just love to move on from quarterbacks who successfully adapt to their system. It is fair to wonder how much Cousins, 38, has left in the tank, but the fact that Teasley actually said this out loud is a little perplexing. At worst, Cousins should be able to serve as a mentor for whichever young quarterback coach Kevin O’Connell decides he wants to whisper to in 2027. Cousins is currently playing on a one-year, $11.3 million contract and could likely be retained on a one- or two-year deal at a similar value.

Headline: Cardinals activated Zach Carter’s 21-day practice window.
News Snippet: Carter has not yet played this season, but he can contribute as a run defender when healthy. The Cardinals also opened Hunter Long’s 21-day practice window, potentially bringing in blocking help for the offense.

Headline: Calvin Ridley said he does not know if he will face charges related to his altercation at the Nashville International Airport.
News Snippet: Ridley told reporters that he was trying to get his keys from the valet at the airport. They were giving him a hard time, so he took the keys out of the valet’s hands. The valet claims the altercation broke his finger. Ridley was at practice today and head coach Robert Saleh called it a “very minor miscommunication.” It doesn’t sound like the incident will keep Ridley off the field for now, though he hasn’t made much of an impact this year anyway.

Headline: Panthers designated Xavier Leggette (knee) to return from injury reserve.
News Snippet: Legette practiced in full, so he could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. He would only return to a part-time role, so there isn’t any fantasy value to be had here. Jonathon Brooks is also practicing, meaning the Panthers’ offense could be getting reinforcements at multiple positions soon.

Headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said the team will stick with Harrison Butker for Week 10 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: Butker has missed a field goal in every game outside of Week 1. His 63 field goal percentage is the worst mark in the league, outside of Harrison Mevis, who is not currently on a roster. Barring a sharp turnaround in Butker’s play, he’ll get benched at some point this year.

Headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said George Pickens (hamstring) is expected to practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: Pickens missed Week 9 with the hamstring issue. He was limited in practice throughout the week, but the team ultimately chose to hold him out for Sunday’s game. We expect one week off to be enough for the veteran wideout. Assuming things go well in practice, Pickens will be back in the WR2 ranks when the Cowboys take on the 49ers.

Headline: Patrick Mahomes (elbow) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: This comes directly from Andy Reid, though we’ll have to wait until the team’s injury report officially drops to be sure it’s actually a full session. Either way, Mahomes is playing on Sunday despite suffering an ugly elbow injury in Week 9. He told reporters it’s simply a matter of pain management for now. The Chiefs may opt to lean on their ground game against the Falcons, but even that won’t knock Mahomes out of the QB1 mix after the addition of Josh Downs.

Headline: Xavier Worthy (hamstring) practiced on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Head coach Andy Reid told reporters Worthy is “actually feeling pretty good.” Worthy went down with a hamstring injury late in the Chiefs’ win over the Jets on Sunday. The fact that he’s able to practice in any capacity today suggests he will be good to go for Week 10 against the Falcons. With Josh Downs now in the mix for targets, Worthy’s days as a relevant fantasy option appear to be over.

Headline: Ravens worked out K Harrison Mevis.
News Snippet: Riley Patterson also worked out for Baltimore. Tyler Loop is on injured reserve and Jake Moody got nabbed off their practice squad, leaving Baltimore without a kicker. One of Mevis or Patterson should get signed in the next few days.

Headline: Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Cashius Howell (wrist) is week-to-week.
News Snippet: Howell injured his wrist in Week 8 and underwent surgery shortly after the game. He was placed on injured reserve last week. Taylor declined to rule him out for the year today but didn’t offer a timeline for his return either. Howell has one tackle and three sacks this year.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Josh Jacobs (finger) could miss 2-3 weeks.
News Snippet: In other words, the Packers might avoid placing Jacobs on injured reserve with his surgically-repaired finger. While he’s sidelined — including in Week 10 against the Vikings — some combination of Pierre Strong, Chris Brooks, Kaleb Johnson, and MarShawn Lloyd will handle backfield duties for the pass-heavy Packers. Johnson served as the nominal lead back in Week 9 against the Patriots, while Brooks is returning from injury and should slot in as the team’s pass-catching back. Johnson can be played as a touchdown-dependent RB3 option this week against a Minnesota defense that has shown recent vulnerabilities to the run.

Headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he expected Treylon Burks (foot) to be active for Week 10 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Burks, according to Quinn, did not practice Wednesday in preparation for Thursday night’s game against the Giants. He missed Week 9 against the Rams with a foot injury. The Commanders’ best downfield threat with Terry McLaurin sidelined, Burks profiles as a high-variance WR4 option this week. The Giants have faced deep passes at the league’s 16th highest rate this season.

Headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said he hopes Malik Willis (groin) can return this season.
News Snippet: Hafley told reporters on Wednesday that Willis would seek second opinions on the groin injury that landed him on injured reserve. It sounds like season-ending surgery is a possibility for Willis, who would end his 2026 campaign. Through Week 9, Willis ranks 26th in passing yardage and 29th in passing touchdowns. He’s dead last in EPA per pass attempt and ranks 28th out of 38 qualifying QBs in EPA per drop back. Kyle McCord will get a chance at quarterback for the Dolphins in Week 10 against the Colts.

Headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said he wasn’t sure if Alec Pierce (heel) will play again this season.
News Snippet: Pierce, who signed a massive new deal with the Colts last offseason, has been on injured reserve since Week 3. The Colts have little reason to rush him back in another lost season. “We’ll see. Like I said last week, he’s still in that rehab process, and I’m not going to put a timetable on return,” Steichen said Wednesday when asked about Pierce’s availability. Steichen mentioned Deion Burks and Anthony Gould as receivers who will see more playing time after the Colts traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen this week.

Headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
News Snippet: It’s a little concerning considering the Titans are coming off their bye week. Tate suffered the shoulder injury three weeks ago, and unless he can log a practice tomorrow or Friday, he’s likely to miss this week’s game aginst the Jaguars. His absence would make Wan’Dale Robinson viable in PPR formats, along with Chimere Dike, who led the Titans in receiving against the Bengals in Week 8.

Headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Omar Cooper, Jr. (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
News Snippet: Cooper is dealing with an ankle issue he suffered in Week 9, but he should be OK for Week 10 against the Bills if he’s able to log a practice on Thursday and/or Friday. Cooper last week against Kansas City led the Jets in targets (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) sidelined. Wilson is expected back for Week 10. Cooper remains a viable flex play in a game that will likely see the Jets play from behind in a potentially pass-heavy game script. Buffalo’s defense has seen the tenth highest pass rate over expected in 2026.

Headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Gould will play slot receiver after Josh Downs was traded to the Chiefs.
News Snippet: With Downs shipped out, the slot role will go to Gould, who has four receptions for 45 yards over three seasons with the Colts. Downs had accounted for 18 percent of the team’s targets and 24 percent of the team’s air yards through Week 9. The Colts use three wideout sets on 59 percent of their offensive plays, the 12th highest rate in the NFL. They rank 29th in EPA per pas attempt with three receivers on the field. Gould should be rostered in deeper formats based on route volume alone.

Headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports Puka Nacua (knee, toe) will not miss the rest of the regular season.
News Snippet: Graziano said there’s an outside chance the Rams won’t put Nacua on injured reserve ahead of Week 10. Rams sources “were very adamant that Nacua’s injury isn’t season-ending and that they hope to get him back around that Week 14, Week 15 time.” With Davante Adams (hamstring) also sidelined, look for the Rams offense to be unusually run heavy in the coming weeks. That should mean more work for Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson could see an uptick in targets too. If Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) is ever able to return to game action, he could profile as the team’s top target. Nacua had seen 44 percent of the Rams’ first-read targets this season, the highest rate in the NFL.

Headline: Cleveland.com’s Mary Kay Cabot reports Deshawn Watson (concussion) will start in Week 10 against the Texans.
News Snippet: Watson was sidelined last week against the Saints with a brain injury. He’ll back in time to face his former team as the Browns push for postseason contention in the competitive NFC North. Shedeur Sanders will revert to his backup role in Week 10 after throwing for 297 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints in an overtime loss. Watson will be a borderline fantasy option against a pass-funnel Texans defense that has allowed the third most air yards per game this season.

Headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports the Giants inquired about Bijan Robinson’s availability before the NFL’s trade deadline.
News Snippet: “They were certainly big game hunting,” Raanan said. Though the thought of the Falcons parting ways with the centerpiece of their offense sounds ridiculous, it’s clear John Harbaugh and the Giants see themselves as a postseason team that won’t be content with a playoff berth. The inquiry on Bijan speaks to the Giants’ ongoing skepticism of Cam Skattebo as a true lead back. The team has done everything they can to prevent Skattebo from taking on a big backfield workload. In Week 10 against the Commanders, with a flurry of backfield injuries and Devin Singletary coming off one of the worst running back performances in NFL history, the Giants might have no choice but to feed Skattebo, who should be started in all 12-team leagues.

Headline: Ravens released TE Nick Vannett.
News Snippet: Vannett joined the Ravens prior to the season and operated as a blocking tight end. He appeared in five games, playing 85 offensive snaps and not seeing a target in the passing games. The Ravens now part ways with Vannett on NFL trade deadline day.

Headline: Rams signed WR Xavier Smith off the 49ers’ practice squad.
News Snippet: With all the injuries at wide receiver, the Rams decide to bring back a familiar face in Xavier Smith in lieu of trading for a receiver. Smith was on the 49ers’ practice squad after the Rams waived him earlier this season. He caught 18 passes for 303 yards for the Rams last year, seeing the bulk of his opportunities as kick returner. Smith figures to operate as receiving depth with special teams utility once again.

Headline: Chig Okonkwo (hip) practiced in full on Tuesday.
News Snippet: That ought to put him firmly in the mix to play on Thursday against the Giants. Okonkwo is coming off a 6/57 game on seven targets against the Rams and figures to again be a reasonable low-end TE1 against the Giants.

Headline: Treylon Burks (foot) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
News Snippet: It’s an upgrade from an estimated DNP on Monday. Dan Quinn has previously said that he’s optimistic Burks will play, but it’s likely that he’ll hit the questionable line tomorrow barring a full practice.

Headline: Cardinals placed QB Gardner Minshew (elbow) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Officially he’ll miss at least four weeks, but Adam Schefter reports he’s not expected to play again this season, which essentially confirms that he tore his UCL without actually confirming it. There’s no current timeline for his return.

Headline: Eagles waived RB Jaydon Blue.
News Snippet: Not the first time this season they’ve done this, so we’re expecting a practice squad reunion here. Blue played eight offensive snaps in two weeks on the active roster and does not need to be on your fantasy team at this point.

Headline: Cowboys signed RB Kendre Miller to their practice squad.
News Snippet: Assuming all goes well, he’ll likely be elevated to be Javonte Williams’ backup this week. Dallas also has Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin as runners on the practice squad, so one of them may also get the first crack at being Williams’ backup as Tyler Goodson nurses a knee injury.

Headline: Vikings released WR Odell Beckham Jr.
News Snippet: Beckham was not targeted in his two offensive snaps yesterday. The idea of Odell Beckham being a good wideout at 34 is really fun, and the reality is that he’s played 22 offensive snaps for two teams this year. Back to the practice squad he goes.

Headline: Rams placed Jordan Whittington (back) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Not the Rams wideout we thought we’d be placing on injured reserve today. Whittington is, nevertheless, another hit to the depth of this wideout corps. It appears to be all systems clear for Konata Mumpfield to be the No. 1 wideout who is tasked with watching Los Angeles’ running backs in Week 10.

Headline: Falcons acquired G Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick from the Ravens for C Ryan Neuzil.
News Snippet: Vorhees, in the final year of his rookie contract, appears to just be in this trade as salary ballast. He struggled in a large sample in 2025 and even with injuries to the interior line in 2026 has only received 81 snaps. The Falcons may opt to turn to Corey Levin as their starter at center rather than Vorhees.

Headline: Ravens acquired C Ryan Neuzil from the Falcons for G Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick.
News Snippet: Neuzil, 29, was in the final year of a two-year extension signed in the 2025 offseason. He’s played reasonably well, with a 77.4 PFF blocking grade in 2025 and a 65.1 blocking grade in 2026. The Ravens, somehow always in need of a center, find a nice piece here at the deadline.

Headline: Darnell Mooney (chest) practiced in full on Tuesday.
News Snippet: We only blurb Mooney injury reports, not Mooney game lines. There’s probably a lesson to be learned from that for fantasy managers.

Headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) practiced in full on Tuesday.
News Snippet: He should be good to go and handle low-end RB2 duties against the Commanders. Seemingly always at his best after a week off — which makes sense due to how physical he plays — don’t be surprised if Skattebo puts up some major fantasy points on Thursday night.

Headline: J.J. McCarthy (hip) practiced in full on Tuesday.
News Snippet: He’ll be ready to take on the Commanders on Thursday night barring a major setback. McCarthy can be penciled in as a mid-range QB2 for the game given the Commanders’ pass-funnel nature.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Titans are holding on to Tony Pollard at the trade deadline.
News Snippet: Keeping a 29-year-old running back on the final year of his contract on your 1-7 cellar franchise is certainly a choice a team is allowed to make. We don’t know if it’s the one we’d make, but Pollard will be here to hover around RB2 value in games the Titans are pesky and RB3 value in games where the Titans offense plays as we’ve come to expect.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Kyle McCord is set to make his NFL debut against the Colts.
News Snippet: McCord! Daniel Jones throwing to Ashton Dulin! All the stars are here in Week 10! Even in an elevated matchup, there’s little reason to believe that McCord will be more than a bottom-five superflex option this week. And this might wind up being one of his good starts, if indeed the Dolphins commit to giving him multiple cracks while Malik Willis is on injured reserve.

Headline: Dolphins placed Malik Willis (groin) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: He had clearly been laboring since the bye week and this will give Willis some time to heal. This is not regarded as a season-ending injury and Willis will be eligible to return in Week 14. In the mean time, it appears we’re all about to see how well the roster cutdown Kyle McCord trade works out for the Dolphins.

Headline: Chiefs acquired WR Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick.
News Snippet: It was an obvious fit. Downs will slot in as Kansas City’s No. 2 wideout behind Rashee Rice and his fantasy stock receives a slight upgrade — though we felt like we’ve spent all year saying that and never seeing any actual returns for it — while Xavier Worthy moves back to the undesirable FLEX shadow zone. The Colts had to make this trade as Downs was a free agent at year’s end, but it has left them with a completely indecipherable wideout room. Ashton Dulin is perhaps the No. 1 target Daniel Jones has outside of Tyler Warren and Jonathan Taylor.

Headline: Panthers released WR David Moore.
News Snippet: He’ll be a candidate for a practice squad spot if he wants to stay. Moore was released to make room for the activation of Xavier Legette off injured reserve.

Headline: Broncos acquired LB Daiyan Henley from the Chargers for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
News Snippet: The Chargers finally make a move, dealing a player who was considered a burgeoning star a few years ago away for a light deadline return. Henley had a career-worst 38.3 PFF coverage grade this year but is still a good tackler and should give the Broncos some oomph on run defense down the stretch.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts won’t trade Jonathan Taylor before today’s trade deadline.
News Snippet: Multiple teams, per Pelissero, offered a second-round pick. It sounds like Indianapolis was holding out for a first. Playing out the season in Indy, Taylor will likely retain RB1 value despite a gross situation. It should be noted that Seth McGowan had begun to cut into Taylor’s playing time a bit, but with the Colts now committed to Taylor for the short-term, it’s plausible that he’ll operate at a 70-75 percent of snaps player for the remainder of the season. McGowan retains contingency value in fantasy leagues but will not stumble into a major role barring injury.

Headline: Jordan Schultz reports the Chargers “immediately shut down all inquiries” for Justin Herbert at the trade deadline.
News Snippet: Schultz reports the Vikings called on Herbert, but the Chargers had no interest in moving on. It’s hard to understand what Herbert’s market value would have been — this has been one of the most disgusting outlier seasons for a previously good quarterback in recent memory — but the Chargers appear ready to move forward with him as their franchise quarterback.

Headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports Kyler Murray (hamstring) is dealing with a grade 2 strain, is “week to week” and is expected to miss more time.
News Snippet: In other words, Kirk Cousins could immediately slide in as the starting quarterback. As for Murray, he appears safe to drop in most formats. Call of Duty released on October 23. Not sure why that appeared in this post, but we seem to be unable to backspace it.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Fernando Mendoza will take over as Raiders starter following the trade of Kirk Cousins to Minnesota.
News Snippet: We’re sure we’ll get something more official from the team once Klint Kubiak has a press conference, but this is the obvious move. The No. 1 overall pick will face a gauntlet in his first three games, starting with the defending champion Seahawks in Week 10. It’s not an immediate re-draft add situations outside of deep leagues, but Mendoza could eventually factor into the re-draft formula this season.

Headline: Vikings acquired QB Kirk Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick.
News Snippet: And where did that bring you? Back to me. Cousins will likely take over as Minnesota’s starting quarterback in the near future, if not immediately. When that happens, Kyler Murray will head back to the bench for a second straight season — he’s droppable in most leagues at this point. Fernando Mendoza will take over as starting quarterback for the Raiders. Mendoza is best approached cautiously at this point in fantasy leagues. Cousins’ value likely remains stagnant — Klint Kubiak was already getting quite a bit out of him — but he provides the Vikings with a better floor at quarterback than what they were getting so it’s obvious after watching Carson Wentz play last night why this is happening.

Headline: Bills acquired S Amani Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Titans for a 2027 second-round pick.
News Snippet: It’s not Budda Baker, but Hooker has a respectable 81.0 PFF defensive grade in 495 snaps this season and has always helped as a run defender. The second-round pick is a steep price to pay and it’s quite a coup for the Titans to get that kind of return, even if they had to throw in another pick to get it done. This is all about solidifying Buffalo’s defense for a Super Bowl run for the Bills.

Headline: 49ers acquired WR Keenan Allen from the Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
News Snippet: Just what the 49ers needed: To get older at the skill positions. With Christian Kirk gone, Allen figures to fill a role for the 49ers and could still be fantasy relevant depending on Mike Evans’ health. It does seem unlikely he’ll draw the same sort of targets as he had been handling for the Colts, but the targets should be more effective. The Colts signed Allen off the street in August and flipped him for something as they realized they were going nowhere, so they’ve done well for themselves here. The wideout vacuum in Indianapolis may draw players like Ashton Dulin into fantasy consideration, especially if Josh Downs also moves later today.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Kirk Cousins is a “prime trade candidate” for the Vikings ahead of today’s trade deadline.
News Snippet: This would, of course, have multiple fantasy impacts. Fernando Mendoza would take over as Las Vegas’ starting quarterback if Cousins were traded, and Kyler Murray would likely take a backseat to Cousins sooner rather than later in Minnesota. We unfortunately must recommend that you stay tuned for the next couple of hours. Click the ads, too.

Headline: Free agent RB Kendre Miller is visiting the Cowboys on Tuesday.
News Snippet: With Tyler Goodson dealing with a knee injury suffered late in Sunday’s game against the Colts, Miller could find himself in a backup role behind Javonte Williams.

Headline: Cardinals signed QB Joey Aguilar off the Jaguars’ practice squad.
News Snippet: With Gardner Minshew looking at a lengthy absence, Aguilar figures to be Arizona’s No. 2 or No. 3 behind Carson Beck for the time being. Aguilar completed 17-of-20 passes for 230 yards and a touchdown in preseason action with the Jaguars after being signed as a UDFA after this year’s draft.

Headline: Falcons released K Nick Folk.
News Snippet: Folk, 42 after his birthday five days ago, had hit just 13-of-18 field-goal attempts this year after being the league’s most accurate kicker in 2023, 2024, and 2025. He’ll either resurface with a new club or have a Bluesky account in the coming days.

Headline: Falcons signed K Jake Moody off Baltimore’s practice squad.
News Snippet: They released Nick Folk in a corresponding move, leaving the Ravens holding nothing at the position currently as Tyler Loop is on injured reserve. Workouts to come for the Ravens. Moody will be a reasonable fantasy kicker provided he can do better than his 78.3 percent career field-goal conversion rate, which, of course, is not guaranteed in any way. At least he plays half his games in a dome now.

Headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Bengals’ trade for Eagles EDGE Arnold Ebiketie has fallen through.
News Snippet: The acquisition had not been finalized, according to Schultz, who said said the nixing of the deal “is not physical or performance related.” It could be related to the Ebiketie acquisition forcing the Bengals to forfeit a 2027 3rd round compensatory draft pick that via the team’s Trey Hendrickson trade to the Ravens. In any case, the Bengals will likely head into the second half of the season with one of the league’s worst pass rushes. Only the Bills and Chiefs have fewer sacks on the season.

Headline: Bengals acquired EDGE Arnold Ebiketie from the Eagles in exchange for 2027 sixth round pick.
News Snippet: The Bengals are shoring up their defense ahead of a postseason run with Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins healthy and operating at a high level. Ebiketie, who had played 48 percent of the Eagles’ defensive snaps this season, logging zero sacks, no tackles for loss, and two QB hits, will join a Bengals defense with the NFL’s tenth highest pressure rate and tenth highest quick pressure rate on the season. Only the Bills and Chiefs have fewer sacks than the Bengals through Week 9.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Dolphins DT Zach Sieler (bicep) is out for the season.
News Snippet: Sieler, who’s played well for an underperforming Miami defense, will undergo surgery on his injured bicep and remain sidelined for the remainder of the regular season. It’s a blow to the Dolphins defense, which has allowed the league’s highest EPA per play and highest offensive success rate. This could make the Dolphins more vulnerable to the run as well. Through Week 9 they have allowed the tenth most fantasy points per game to running backs, along with the 13th highest yards per carry.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Jaguars won’t trade Brian Thomas, Jr. ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline.
News Snippet: Fowler said the Jacksonville front office has told other teams they will not part ways with Thomas before today’s 4:00 eastern trade deadline. Thomas, 24, has been an afterthought in the Jaguars offense for much of the 2026 season after a down 2025 campaign. He’s run a route on 47 percent of the team’s drop backs while accounting for 9 percent of the team’s targets and 16 percent of the team’s air yards. Thomas has seen a target on 17 percent of his pass routes, the sixth highest rate among Jags pass catchers. Stuck in Jacksonville, Thomas will have some deep league value as a big play dependent wideout.

Headline: The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman believes Kaleb Johnson could have a chance to be the Packers’ lead rusher in the coming weeks.
News Snippet: With Josh Jacobs out with a broken finger, Johnson led the Packers with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the team’s Week 9 drubbing of the Patriots. Forty-four of those yards came on explosive rushes. Pierre Strong, meanwhile had eight carries on the day. MarShawn Lloyd was sidelined with a knee issue but could be back in the Green Bay lineup soon. Lloyd’s shocking lack of production this season could, according to Schneidman, give Johnson a real chance to seize lead back duties. Head coach Matt LaFleur after the team’s Week 9 win seemed to imply there are some pass protection concerns for Johnson. That would probably mean Chris Brooks, who’s expected to return from an ankle injury in Week 10, gets the third-down role while Jacobs is sidelined. The Packers this week take on an elite Minnesota offense that teams have run on in recent weeks.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Vikings could trade for a quarterback before the NFL’s trade deadline.
News Snippet: “The word going into last night was the Vikings would be in the QB market ahead of the trade deadline if Carson Wentz didn’t play well,” Garafolo said. Narrator voice: He didn’t. Wentz was an utter disaster in Monday night’s loss to the Bills, completing 8-of-25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the team’s second straight loss. Wentz in Week 9 had the league’s lowest drop back EPA and lowest success rate. He also appeared to sustain an ankle injury in the second half. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) struggling mightily in Kevin O’Connell’s offense, the Vikings could make a desperation move for Kirk Cousins or Daniel Jones ahead of today’s 4:00 p.m. eastern time trade deadline. Cousins, for one, would be a marked upgrade for Justin Jefferson and the Minnesota pass catchers. The Raiders have not expressed interest in parting with Cousins, however.

Headline: Jordan Addison caught 2-of-3 targets for 28 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Addison and the rest of the primary Minnesota pass catchers struggled through some of the worst quarterback play you will see all season, with Carson Wentz leading an offense that gained only 126 yards while failing to pick up a single first down through 55 minutes of play. Max Brosmer came on in relief of the struggling veteran late in the fourth quarter and made a few really nice throws, but the team maintains one of the worst quarterback rooms in the league. Fantasy managers are left wishing the team addresses those shortcomings ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline to revive an anemic pass offense.

Headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-7 targets for 33 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: Hockenson struggled along with the rest of a Minnesota offense that managed only 178 yards of total offense, only 126 of which were accounted for with Carson Wentz under center. Max Brosmer came on in relief of the beleaguered veteran on the team’s final possession an nearly led the only touchdown drive of the game, ultimately coming up short on fourth down in the red zone. Hockenson and the rest of the Minnesota pass catchers are surely better off with any other quarterback than is currently on the roster, and there is the potential for the team to address the poor under-center play in the coming hours ahead of Tuesday’s 4 pm ET trade deadline. Hockenson would be a tough fantasy start against the Packers in Week 10 if the situation remains the same.

Headline: Justin Jefferson caught 3-of-11 targets for 58 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills.
News Snippet: It was a game to forget for Jefferson and the Vikings, who gained only 178 yards of total offense on just over 17 minutes in time of possession. Jefferson also failed to secure what was initially ruled on incomplete pass on a screen attempt in the first half, later overturned to a Carson Wentz fumble after being ruled a backwards pass. Furthering the pain for Jefferson’s fantasy managers is the fact that 19 of his yards came on the team’s final possession with Max Brosmer under center, leaving arguably the most talented wide receiver in the league completely bereft of a viable option at quarterback considering Wentz’s struggles. His fantasy contingency are best off saying their prayers that the team decides to address the quarterback position in the next 17 hours ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. Jefferson would be a middling WR2 if the position remains unchanged ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Packers.

Headline: Aaron Jones rushed five times for 16 yards in the Vikings’ Week 9 loss to the Bills, adding five yards on one reception.
News Snippet: Jones’ six opportunities were three behind backfield-mate Jordan Mason, despite the former getting the start on paper.
