This was particularly painful for fantasy managers when he got near the end zone. Judkins was stuffed from the one- and three-yard line on separate drives. He also ceded receiving work to Dylan Sampson. Judkins was targeted once while Sampson saw six opportunities through the air. Without receiving work to buoy his poor rushing days, Judkins is tumbling down the RB2 ranks. He’ll be on the RB2/3 border for his Week 10 matchup with the Texans.

Headline: Drew Lock completed 19-of-28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ 17-3, Week 9 win over the Cardinals, adding 16 yards on five carries.
News Snippet: Lock appeared to suffer discomfort in the third quarter following an incomplete pass attempt, holding his side or oblique and grimacing in pain as he made his way to sideline. He would get checked in the medical tent but returned without missing a down. Lock looked poised in the pocket and in control of the offense throughout, leaning on his alpha wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba early before the team went into preservation mode with a sizable lead in the second half. Lock could be looking at another start or two, pending the length of recovery from a cracked rib for Sam Darnold. The team passed an update on Lock’s oblique injury following the game, indicating that the veteran journeyman would undergo follow-on testing but that his status for Week 10 could be in doubt.

Headline: Drake Maye completed 21-of-38 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions in the Patriots’ 45-27, Week 9 loss to the Packers.
News Snippet: Maye’s three first-half interceptions but the Patriots in the hole early, but the defenses’ inability to limit explosive plays also didn’t do them any favors. The Patriots saw three of their first six drives end in interceptions, but Maye did what he could to keep the game within reach. He completed his first touchdown pass of the day to Rhamondre Stevenson, who broke free down field for the 30-yard score in the second quarter. and on the following drive, Maye would complete passes of 19 and 28 yards to set up Efton Chism for an eight-yard touchdown with less than three minutes to go in the half. His third and final touchdown would come on a 22-yard pass to Mack Hollins, but Maye and the Patriots were under duress all afternoon and struggled to keep up with a Packers offense that didn’t slow down until it pulled it’s starters late in the fourth quarter. Maye also took four sacks in this one and has now been sacked nine times in his last three games. He’ll look to bounce back next week against the Lions in Munich.

Headline: Jordan Love completed 23-of-29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns in the Packers’ 45-27, Week 9 win over the Patriots.
News Snippet: As has been the case for much of the season, big plays were the name of the game for Love. Love aired the ball out at will against a helpless Patriots defense, going 6-for-9 on passes of 20-plus air yards for 235 yards and a touchdown. Love connected with Matthew Golden on multiple long plays in the first quarter, completing passes of 43 and 49 yards, and found him in the end zone for a five-yard score. Love’s longest touchdown pass of the day came in the third quarter when he connected with Christian Watson for a 39-yard-score immediately after the Packers recovered a fumble by Rhamondre Stevenson. Love and the Packers boast arguably the most explosive passing attack in the league, and both Watson and Golden continue to look like premier threats while also being versatile in other areas of the field. Love and the Vikings will have their work cut out for them next week at home against the Vikings, but he will remain in the QB1 mix.

Headline: Trey McBride caught 7-of-8 targets for 54 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
News Snippet: The lone incompletion directed toward McBride came on the team’s final play of the game when the veteran tight end was unable to corral an end zone target that was thrown slightly behind him on fourth and goal. McBride combined with alpha wide receiver Michael Wilson to account for 15 targets on 30 Minshew pass attempts, something we’d expect to continue forward give the current state of the team. The Cardinals get another difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 10, where McBride will remain a surefire TE1 in fantasy circles.

Headline: Michael Wilson caught 6-of-7 targets for 60 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks.
News Snippet: The lone Gardner Minshew incompletion directed toward Wilson was an end zone target late in the fourth quarter, a miss that would have salvaged a usable fantasy outing for the veteran receiver. Wilson was responsible for nearly one third of the total offensive output from a Cardinals offense that was held to under 200 yards by the stingy Seattle defense, finishing second on the team in targets behind the eight of tight end Trey McBride. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of another difficult test against the Rams in Week 10.

Headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed 17 times for 46 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, gaining zero additional yards on two receptions.
News Snippet: In what was the first game as the clear starter for the Cardinals in the absence of both Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight, Allgeier was contained to only 2.7 yards per carry as the offense managed under 200 yards of total offense against the stingy Seattle defense. Fantasy managers that were quick to scoop Allgeier off of waivers heading into Week 9 are surely to be disappointed with the returns, particularly considering Knight had largely outperformed the former prior to missing Week 9 with a concussion. Expect a near-even split backfield once Knight returns, which appears likely to be in Week 10 when the Cardinals face another difficult test in the Rams.

Headline: Gardner Minshew completed 21-of-30 passes for 166 yards in the Cardinals’ 17-3, Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, adding four yards on one carry.
News Snippet: To be fair, the matchup in Week 9 was far different than the one Minshew erupted in last week, with the Seattle defense placing the clamps on the Cardinals from the first kick, holding them to just 198 total yards of offense on the down night. The only points mustered came on the team’s first possession, with three of their five first half possessions resulting in three-and-outs. The Cardinals saw the football only thrice following the break, getting stopped after achieving first and goal from the four on their final possession of the game. It was an outing to forget for all parties. Minshew remains likely to be the starting quarterback, at least in the immediate future, but the looking presence of rookie Carson Beck could be accelerated if the former returns more games like this one. Up next for the Cardinals are the Rams in Week 10, where Minshew will be nothing more than a streamer in two-quarterback leagues.

Headline: Greg Dulcich caught 2-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: Despite the quiet fantasy outing, Dulcich finished second on the team in catches and yards. If you couldn’t tell, it was not a productive day for Miami’s passing attack. Dulcich had stacked a few usable weeks over the past month, but Week 9 was his breakout spot against a dreadful Detroit defense. Having missed his big opportunity, he’ll return to the back of the TE2 ranks for Week 10 against the Colts.

Headline: Ashton Jeanty had six rushes for 25 yards in the Raiders’ Week 9 loss to the 49ers, adding five catches for -5 yards.
News Snippet: Jeanty and Mike Washington were scripted out in the second half, with the Raiders — as usual — falling behind by multiple scores. Jeanty was swallowed up by Niners defenders almost every time he caught the ball in the backfield. The plodding Jeanty couldn’t get anything going against a swarming 49ers defense. This was Jenaty’s sixth game of the season with at least four catches. It’s a role that has made him playable in 12-team leagues this season. Washington, meanwhile, had six carries for -3 yards. Jeanty might have some flex value in Week 10 against the Seahawks.

Headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) will not return in the Patriots’ Week 9 game against the Packers.
News Snippet: Stevenson suffered his knee injury late in the third quarter, but was eventually able to make it to the field under his own power. After spending a few moments in the blue medical tent, Stevenson went to the locker room and was ruled out soon after by the team. The 28-year-old back managed just 32 scoreless yards on six carries, but hauled in a 30-yard reception from Drake Maye in the second quarter, finishing the day with a 3-46-1 line on four targets. With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined with neurological concerns, the Patriots could be looking at using Corey Kiner as their top back entering Week 10 against the Lions.

Headline: Dallas Goedert caught 5-of-6 targets for 50 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
News Snippet: With No. 3 QB Joe Milton making his starting debut, Goedert padded the box score with some empty PPR production. Excellent, though there figures to be distressingly little difference between Goedert’s floor and ceiling for the time being. With the Eagles headed on bye for Week 10, how Goedert is valued upon the team’s return will depend on whether DeVonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks finally get back in the lineup.

Headline: Brock Purdy completed 17-of-25 attempts for 232 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 9 win against the Raiders, adding seven rushes for 40 yards and a touchdown.
News Snippet: Purdy made quick work of a Raiders defense that has ranked as one of the NFL’s worst over the past month. The Niners tormented the Vegas defense with well-timed screens and quick hits to the middle of the field. Purdy used his legs in a couple high leverage situations in the first half and scored his second rushing touchdown of the season. He connected with Christian McCaffrey and Jordan Watkins for his throwing scores. The ultra-efficient Purdy will take on the generationally bad Dallas defense in Week 10.

Headline: Chris Bell failed to catch his only target in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: With nine targets over his previous two games, Bell looked to be building some momentum headed into Week 9. Instead, he posted the dreaded goose egg. The good news is that Bell ran a route on 77 percent of Malik Willis’s dropbacks. He’s running as the team’s WR3, but there’s barely enough passing volume to keep the WR1 in the FLEX mix. Bell remains an interesting dynasty stash, but he is not on the redraft radar headed into Week 10.

Headline: Makai Lemon caught 6-of-9 targets for 61 yards in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
News Snippet: Lemon again led this limited offense in receiving as Joe Milton made his first start under center, but he hurt the cause with a handful of drops, including a particularly brutal one with the Eagles desperately trying to tie the game late. Lemon now has at least six catches in three straight games but has not reached 70 yards in the process. In other words, he is posting empty PPR volume. That will remain the “thesis of the play” when the Eagles come off bye in Week 11, though the return of either DeVonta Smith or Dontayvion Wicks would take a major bite out of Lemon’s WR3 appeal.

Headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (undisclosed) exited in the third quarter of Week 9’s game against the Patriots and went to the locker room.
News Snippet: Stevenson was slow to get up after a play late in the third quarter and was seen going to the locker room shortly after leaving the field. He spent some time in the blue medical tent, but the team has not disclosed what he is dealing with. Stevenson has rushed six times for 32 yards so far and has caught another three passes for 46 yards and a touchdown.

Headline: Malik Washington caught 2-of-3 targets for 21 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 9 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: Washington wasn’t awfully involved in this game, even if you account for the Dolphins’ low-volume passing approach. He earned a 12 percent target share and added one carry for zero yards. Caleb Douglas, on the other hand, was the runaway WR1 for Miami. He earned eight targets and led the team with six grabs for 70 yards. Already completely out of the playoff race, the Dolphins are in evaluation mode with their young receiver corps. That could mean increasing workloads for Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman. Washington will get another week in the WR4 ranks, but he could be waiver wire fodder if he posts another quiet game against the Colts next week.

Headline: Courtland Sutton caught 5-of-9 targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers.
News Snippet: Even with Pat Bryant (ankle) returning, Sutton posted new season highs for receptions and targets as Jaylen Waddle departed early with a concussion. He did get out-gained by Bryant, who also found the end zone. Sutton is a perfectly fine role player, but it is the bitter truth that he is no longer a featured option. With Waddle now having the Broncos’ bye week to get healthy, Sutton could be returning as the team’s No. 3 option. He’s a borderline WR4/5 hold in leagues with shallower benches.

Headline: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-5 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers.
News Snippet: Active for the first time since Week 4, a returning Bryant (ankle) ended up leading the Broncos in receiving. Jaylen Waddle was forced to depart after only one target with a concussion. Bryant’s score, his second of the season, was a 26-yarder against broken coverage. Although his snaps were somewhat rationed following his month-long layoff, Bryant avoided setbacks and continues to look like a dark horse contender for No. 1 receiver duties in Denver. He’s a solid bench option heading into the Broncos’ Week 10 bye before their Week 11 return against the Raiders.

Headline: Darren Waller caught 8-of-10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
News Snippet: By far the best game of Waller’s first season in Carolina came as Tommy Tremble also found the end zone. The duo combined for 12 catches as Bryce Young flooded the middle of the field with looks. Good stuff if you were forced to take a TE2 dart throw, but this is the first time since Week 3 Waller has seen genuine volume. We would consider it a one-off spiked week heading into an admittedly plus Week 10 date in the Saints.

Headline: Justin Herbert entered the blue medical tent in Week 9 against the Texans after suffering an apparent left hand injury.
News Snippet: Herbert appeared to injure his left hand, and specifically his left middle finger, while fending off a pass rusher in the fourth quarter. He fractured the same hand, and seemingly the same digit, last year and underwent surgery to stabilize it in-season. We tentatively expect him to return after getting it taped up, but he will be playing hurt.

Headline: Jalen Coker caught 4-of-5 targets for 29 yards in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
News Snippet: Coker is now really going through it over his past three games, managing just seven total catches for 74 yards and a touchdown. If there’s “good” news, it’s that it has been an offensive-wide slump in Carolina, not just Coker. He and everyone else has a premium Week 10 get-right spot in the Saints, though Coker is starting to look more like a WR3 than the WR2 he was showing out as earlier in the year.

Headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is active for Week 9 against the Bears.
News Snippet: As expected, Egbuka is back after missing two games with his foot injury. The wideout has been heavily targeted when healthy, but hasn’t been particularly effective with those opportunities with zero games over 65 yards in 2026. The Bucs’ inactives for Week 9 will be OLB Yaya Diaby, G Trevor Keegan, G Billy Schrauth, CB Ayden Garnes and DL DeMonte Capehart.

Headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 4-of-6 targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos.
News Snippet: McMillan’s four-yard touchdown with the Panthers attempting to complete a fourth quarter comeback was his first since Week 4 and only his third of the season. He has also now been held below 60 yards receiving in three straight games as Bryce Young has been mired in a slump. If there’s good news, it’s that McMillan has maintained a decent floor, and we know the next spiked week can’t be far away. It could come as early as Week 10 against the Saints’ soft defense.

Headline: Malik Willis completed 13-of-25 passes for 128 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 19-9, Week 9 loss to the Lions.
News Snippet: Willis only added seven yards on two carries. He was on the injury report with a groin injury this week. Despite practicing in full three times, Willis appeared to be severely limited by the issue. He turned down several opportunities to scramble, instead opting to throw the ball away when the Lions’ pass-rush got close. Without the rushing production to bail him out of tough spots, the offense collapsed despite facing one of the league’s worst defenses. His passing output was already weak, but a lack of rush attempts will pull him out of the QB2 ranks entirely. He will be downgraded to a low-end QB2 for his Week 10 matchup with the Colts.

Headline: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
News Snippet: Although this was a step back on Fields’ pre-bye performance of 4/83, it was actually only the second time all season he caught more than two passes. He continues to head in the right direction as J.J. McCarthy provides some upside hope for this offense. That being said, McCarthy’s (hip) status is questionable for Thursday against the Commanders, while Fields has still not proven his WR4 bonafides. He mostly remains an end-of-bench stash in conventional 12-team leagues.

Headline: Malik Nabers caught 5-of-8 targets for 43 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
News Snippet: Entering the game with four straight 100-yard performances, Nabers had a day of what ifs. Banged up early but no worse for the wear, Nabers played snaps with two different QBs as J.J. McCarthy missed part of the third quarter with a hip issue. McCarthy returned only for Nabers to drop a should-have-been 20-yard touchdown in the end zone. Frustrating, but 9.43 PPR points on a “down” day is not the worst outcome. Nabers and McCarthy have only four days to heal up for Thursday’s short-week date with the Commanders, but Nabers’ status is not in doubt, while he will remain a high-end WR1 even if Jameis Winston returns under center for the G-Men.

Headline: Isaiah Likely caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
News Snippet: Although it was another down day in the yardage department by his recent standards, Likely got the fantasy job done with his score and five receptions. It also wasn’t a bad outcome in a contest where J.J. McCarthy missed time with a hip injury and the Giants attempted only 27 throws vs. a reeling Eagles team. Likely’s touchdown was a five-yarder where he took advantage of mass defensive confusion at the goal line. It is unclear if McCarthy will be ready for Thursday’s short-week date with the Commanders, but Likely will remain a high-end QB1 even if Jameis Winston returns under center.

Headline: Jared Goff completed 17-of-25 passes for 170 yards and an interception in the Lions’ 19-9, Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: The Lions undoubtedly played down to their opponents in this game, putting up six points in the first half before finding slightly more success after the break. Things got off to a rocky start with an easy interception for Dolphins defensive back Chris Johnson. Goff was hit as he threw the ball and it wobbled right into Johnson’s arms. The Lions had one drive go for more than 50 yards. Jahmyr Gibbs punched in the score at the end of the drive, taking home the only Lions touchdown of the day. Goff should have no issues turning things around against the Patriots next week. He will remain near the top of the QB1 ranks for Week 10.

Headline: Emmett Johnson had six rushes for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets.
News Snippet: Johnson, fresh off a big receiving day in Week 8 against the Broncos, didn’t see much involvement until the Chiefs were up multiple scores in the fourth quarter. He ran in his first NFL touchdown on a goal line carry after Ken Walker — who had three touchdowns on the day — was resting on the sideline. Johnson remains one of the game’s most important and upside backup running backs and should be rostered in every league in case Walker misses time.

Headline: Mason Taylor caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
News Snippet: Taylor ran a route on 22 of the team’s 39 drop backs while Kenyon Sadiq has 21 routes and caught all four of his targets. Splitting the TE1 role with Sadiq, Taylor won’t be fantasy viable in most formats next week against the Bills. He has four receptions over his past two games.

Headline: Sam LaPorta caught 4-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: LaPorta was the only Lion outside of Amon-Ra St. Brown to catch more than two passes. He accounted for a fifth of Jared Goff’s targets, but the team’s low-volume passing approach meant there wasn’t much volume to go around. LaPorta has gone cold in recent weeks with three straight games under 40 yards. He’ll look to get back on track as a mid-range TE1 versus the Patriots next week.

Headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: Sadiq logged 21 pass routes on the day to Mason Taylor’s 22 routes. The two tight ends have largely split the TE1 role in the New York offense in recent weeks. Taylor had just one catch on two targets against Kansas City, while Sadiq got open down the seam a couple times and found himself wide open for Geno Smith. Sadiq, who had five receptions over his previous four outings, won’t be usable in most fantasy formats next week against the Bills.

Headline: Saquon Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 9 loss to the Giants.
News Snippet: It was a horribly inefficient day for the Eagles’ superstar back, but there was not a whole lot he could do with the Giants understandably not respecting the “threat” presented by No. 3 Philly quarterback Joe Milton. Barkley at least saved face with his three-yard scoring plunge in the first quarter. Having his snaps and touches rationed for this injury-ruined and tanking team, Barkley will probably have a hard time getting back into the RB1 ranks when Philly comes off bye in Week 11 against the Steelers.

Headline: Xavier Worthy sustained a hamstring injury in Week 9 against the Jets.
News Snippet: Worthy hobbled off the field after a fourth quarter reception in the KC victory. It appeared to be the serious kind of hamstring injury but we won’t know the extent of it until the team tests the speedy receiver. Worthy had caught all six of his targets for 48 yards before exiting the game. An absence of Worthy would likely free up more targets for Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice. The team’s running backs could also see an uptick in targets if Worthy misses time.

Headline: Jameson Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for 31 yards in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: We’re not sure if a player can be due for a catastrophic bust of a fantasy week, but “Jamo” was probably due for a catastrophic bust. He came into this game red hot, with 208 yards and five touchdowns over his past three games. Given Williams boom/bust nature, a flop was always right around the corner. He also dropped one of his two targets, which didn’t help his cause. The Lions get a potential shootout with the Patriots next week, meaning fantasy managers can safely keep Williams in their lineups as a WR3 despite today’s quiet outing.

Headline: Chuba Hubbard rushed 16 times for 79 yards in the Panthers’ Week 9 loss to the Broncos, adding four receptions for 17 yards.
News Snippet: Hubbard’s 16 totes were his second fewest since Week 2, though fantasy managers will at least take the 96 yards from scrimmage. Handling huge workloads and snap counts, Hubbard hasn’t always maintained his efficiency under such voluminous usage, though we have yet to see any red flags in 2026. He will remain a strong option on the RB1/2 borderline for Week 10 against the Saints.

Headline: J.K. Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers, adding a four-yard reception.
News Snippet: Dobbins operated as a pure breather back for this one, getting out-touched 21-5 by Jonah Coleman and out-snapped 58-11. Dobbins did receive two touches inside the Panthers’ 20-yard line — one of which was nullified by penalty — but none inside the 10. It sure looks as if the Broncos are ready to ride rookie Coleman, making Dobbins a shaky 12-team league hold since the Broncos are now headed on bye. They return in Week 11 against the Raiders. The odds are strong Dobbins will not be in your starting lineup for that one.

Headline: Jonah Coleman rushed 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 9 win over the Panthers, adding four receptions for 31 yards.
News Snippet: Coleman also put the ball on the ground near his own goal line on a Bo Nix pitch, but the Broncos were thankfully able to recover. Also thankfully for fantasy managers, coach Sean Payton continued to look Coleman’s way late after the miscue, including the very next play. Coleman experienced really strong usage in Charlotte, playing 58-of-75 snaps per PFF’s initial count while easily setting a new career high with his 21 touches. He has also now cleared 80 yards from scrimmage in back-to-back contests. It must be noted that today’s score was not a goal-line carry — it came from nine yards out — but he did receive a first quarter carry from the Panthers’ four-yard line. Coleman’s role continues to grow, thus far without setback. Hopefully that does not change when the Broncos come off bye in Week 11 against the Raiders’ soft defense. We will be ranking Coleman as a strong RB2 for that one.

Headline: Greg Desrosiers rushed three times for 20 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles.
News Snippet: The Giants’ “No. 2 running back” with Cam Skattebo (hamstring) on the shelf, Desrosiers was charted as playing only five snaps, but his 20 yards on three touches were just 19 fewer than Devin Singletary generated on 23 handles. Translation, if Skattebo can’t go for Thursday evening’s short-week date with the Commanders, UDFA Desrosiers might be in line for more work following Singletary’s stink bomb against the Eagles. That’s a 14-team league waivers dart calling your name.

Headline: Ashton Dulin caught 1-of-2 targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Dulin’s lone reception went for a 55-yard touchdown on a simple screen late in the third quarter to bring the Colts within three, but it likely came with the veteran journeyman sitting on waiver wires. Dulin is a name to keep an eye on ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline as his role could be growing, pending what the team does with Josh Downs.

Headline: Josh Downs caught 3-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Downs saw numerous snaps in coverage by his younger brother, Caleb Downs, and was unable to return a usable fantasy outing for the seventh time in nine appearances for the Colts this season. The subject of significant trade speculation ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline, Downs appears likely to be headed for a change of scenery in a contract year, with the Colts reportedly already holding an offer in hand. More to come from one of fantasy’s most disappointing mid-round selections.

Headline: Devin Singletary rushed 21 times for 31 yards in the Giants’ Week 9 win over the Eagles, adding two receptions for eight yards.
News Snippet: Charted by Pro Football Focus as playing 62-of-67 snaps with Cam Skattebo (hamstring) on the shelf, Singletary was an every-down player, but a predictably ineffective one. In fact, his performance was just the third time this decade a player generated fewer than 40 yards from scrimmage on 20-plus touches. The 29-year-old lost what little remained of his explosiveness several years ago, and should never end up in a position where he is “forced” to be an every-down back. With Skattebo supposedly “pushing to play” this afternoon, hopefully he will be ready for Thursday evening’s short-week date with the Commanders. If not, Singletary will be a low-upside FLEX who might cede more snaps and touches to rookie UDFA Greg Desrosiers.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Puka Nacua (knee) will undergo an MRI on Monday.
News Snippet: Rams fans and fantasy managers will be holding their collective breath as they await the results of tomorrow’s MRI. According to Garafolo, Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap of the game when he took a rush attempt for five yards before the Rams punted the ball away. Nacua took a low hit from Commanders safety Jeremy Reaves, but didn’t appear to suffer a serious injury in real time. Garafolo reports, “the team does not believe [Nacua] suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more.” It goes without saying that the Rams can ill-afford to lose another receiver, especially one of Nacua’s caliber. We will be sure to check back in with any updates on his injury as they come.

Headline: Geno Smith completed 18-of-32 attempts for 162 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding one rush for eight yards.
News Snippet: The 36-year-old Smith was as immobile as ever, taking five sacks on the day and narrowly avoiding a half dozen others. Some of that was the Jets offensive line being overwhelmed against an elite KC pass rush; some of it was Smith refusing to get rid of the ball as the pocket collapsed. Smith playing without Garrett Wilson (concussion) was irate on the sideline in the fourth quarter with the Jets down multiple scores, barking at coaches and teammates alike. He had a negative EPA per drop back on the day. Smith should be seen as a matchup-dependent fantasy play. He will be streamable in Week 10 against a vulnerable Buffalo secondary.

Headline: Keenan Allen caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Allen wasn’t targeted until late in the second quarter but picked up two receptions on back-to-back plays to tease fantasy managers in an otherwise poor outing. Things can’t get much worse in Indianapolis, with their decisions in the coming days ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline potentially allowing Allen to step into a more featured role in the second half of the season. Stay tuned as the Colts limp into a Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins.

Position: Concepcion caught 4-of-6 targets for 85 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
Headline: KC Concepcion caught 4-of-6 targets for 85 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 9 loss to the Saints.
News Snippet: Concepcion’s day appeared to be over late in the third quarter when he limped off the field with a non-contact injury. Concepcion was unable to put any weight on his leg and needed to be helped off the field by trainers. He was then on the field to return a punt ahead of Cleveland’s next drive. The rookie made it stunningly clear that he was fine in the fourth quarter with a 64-yard receiving touchdown. Sanders hit him for a long gain and Concepcion outran two Saints defenders for his first career touchdown. With 221 receiving yards over his past three games, Concepcion is heating up just in time for the fantasy playoff hunt. He will be in the WR3 mix versus the Texans next week.

Headline: Tyler Warren caught 4-of-7 targets for 44 yards in the Colts’ Week 9 loss to the Cowboys.
News Snippet: Warren wasn’t targeted in the first half as the team struggled to move the football consistently, catching his first ball on the team’s second possession of the third quarter. The Colts limp toward Tuesday’s trade deadline with numerous key players the subject of trade speculation, of which quarterback Daniel Jones, wide receiver Josh Downs, and running back Jonathan Taylor are amongst. Which is to say, Warren’s fantasy expectations could be heavily influenced by the team’s actions in the coming days, potentially setting the second-year tight end up to be the team’s top option during the second half of the season. Warren would appear to be in a solid spot on paper against the Dolphins in Week 10, where his fantasy value will be dependent on who remains with the team through Tuesday.

Headline: Braelon Allen had eight rushes for 23 yards in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs, adding two catches for 21 yards.
News Snippet: Breece Hall, returning from his quad injury, led the New York backfield with 15 carries while adding three grabs out of the backfield. It was Allen, however, who led the Jets backfield in pass routes, 21 to 10. That sort of pass game usage could keep Allen viable in deeper formats since the Jets are going to be chasing points more weeks than not. Both Jets running backs average 4.1 yards per carry against an elite KC front seven. Allen plays the Bills in Week 10.

Headline: Stefon Diggs caught 3-of-5 targets for 51 yards in the Commanders’ Week 9 loss to the Rams.
News Snippet: With the Commanders down three receivers, Diggs appeared prime for a decent day against a Rams secondary that was down two corners. Instead, the 32-year-old receiver was outshone by journeyman Van Jefferson for most of the day until the final drive of the game. With the Commanders looking to mount a game-tying drive, Diggs broke free into the secondary to make a 42-yard reception, which accounted for nearly all of his receiving production. In two games without Terry McLaurin, Diggs has averaged just 5.5 targets per game and totaled 89 yards and a touchdown. He’s far from the target hog he was in his prime, and shouldn’t be treated as anything more than a WR3/WR4 on Thursday night against the Giants.

Headline: Adonai Mitchell didn’t catch any of his seven targets in the Jets’ Week 9 loss to the Chiefs.
News Snippet: A week after going ballistic against the Raiders, the high-variance Mitchell couldn’t come up with a grab in an embarrassing effort for a Jets offense that was without Garrett Wilson (concussion). If your fantasy league awards points for air yards, Mitchell would have been a week winner against Kansas City. Alas, he could not convert any of that opportunity into real-life production, though he came awfully close on a couple well-thrown Geno Smith downfield balls.

Headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 23-of-41 attempts for 242 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 9 win against the Jets, adding two rushes for eight yards.
News Snippet: Mahomes was pulled with a few minutes to go in the fourth quarter with the Chiefs up multiple scores and the Jets not all that interested in staging a comeback. Mahomes overcame an injury to his right forearm in this one. He sustained the injury on a hard hit from a blitzing New York defender who bent Mahomes’ arm back awkwardly. After getting some treatment on the sideline, Mahomes re-entered the game and seemed fine, though he was seen grimacing and shaking his arm at times. This marked Mahomes’ sixth multi-touchdown game of the season. He should remain in starting lineups as a top-12 option in Week 10 against the pass-funnel Atlanta defense.

Headline: Jahmyr Gibbs rushed 20 times for 74 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 9 win over the Dolphins.
News Snippet: This was easily Gibbs’ worst fantasy outing of the year, though that largely speaks to just how incredible he has been in 2026. The big difference today was a lack of receiving usage. Gibbs was only targeted once and failed to catch a pass for the first time since Week 4 of the 2024 season. Jared Goff only attempted 25 passes, but that would still result in more than one target for Gibbs on a normal day. We’re willing to write this off as the product of a low-scoring rock fight with the Dolphins. Gibbs will be back at the top of the RB1 ranks for his Week 10 date game against the Patriots.

Headline: Raiders declared DT Thomas Booker, WR Malik Benson, WR Dont’e Thornton, G Bryce Cabeldue, SAF Dalton Johnson, and QB Aidan O’Connell inactive for Week 9 against the 49ers.
News Snippet: The struggling Vegas defense will be without Booker against the ultra-efficient 49ers offense. The Raiders since Week 4 has allowed the NFL’s third highest EPA per rush and the fifth highest rushing success rate. That should be good news for both Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black.

Headline: Jake Ferguson (knee) is questionable to return to Week 9 against the Colts.
News Snippet: The term “questionable” is a vast understatement based on the replay, although the veteran tight end did walk off the field under his own power. The replay and initial reaction from Ferguson did not look good. Expect an update from the team following the game. Ferguson caught both targets for 21 yards and a touchdown prior to departing.

Headline: J.J. McCarthy (hip, questionable) returned before the end of the third quarter in the Giants’ Week 9 game against the Eagles.
News Snippet: McCarthy, who presumably received some sort of pain-killing injection after twice collapsing in the third quarter, returned for the final play of the frame. He screamed at his offensive linemen to pump them up before doing so. Never a dull moment.

Headline: 49ers declared WR Mike Evans, WR Deebo Samuel, QB Kurtis Rourke, OT Enrique Cruz, LB Tatum, Bethune, and DL Khalid Kareem inactive for Week 9 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: Evans will miss at least one game with his lingering Achilles injury. Look for the Niners to be careful with their WR1 in the coming weeks. Demarcus Robinson, coming off an injury, will return to the lineup against Vegas and likely operate as the Niners’ top wideout. Robinson will be flex-viable against a porous Vegas secondary.

Headline: J.J. McCarthy suffered a hip injury in the Giants’ Week 9 game against the Eagles and is questionable to return.
News Snippet: Jameis Winston, of course, is now in the game. McCarthy took a thunderclap third quarter hit from Eagles LB Zack Baun and struggled to his feet. He attempted to warm back up on the sideline before literally collapsing while trying to throw. He then headed to the blue tent before making his way to the locker room. We suppose he is genuinely questionable, but on the wrong side of the tag. McCarthy had been taking an absolute beating before going down, absorbing five sacks, many of which were of the spine-rattling variety.

Headline: Broncos CB Riley Moss suffered a concussion in Denver’s Week 9 game against the Panthers and will not return.
News Snippet: Attempting to help out in run defense, Moss took a second quarter knee to the hit and went down in extremely concerning fashion. He was ruled out after the break. The Broncos’ thinned out pass defense has been struggling since Moss’ departure.

Headline: Seahawks declared QB Sam Darnold, WR Rashid Shaheed, T Charles Cross, G Quenton Nelson, LB Uchenna Nwosu, DT Brandon Pili, and DT Leonard Williams inactive for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
News Snippet: Darnold was ruled out earlier in the week while Shaheed misses his second consecutive game with a knee injury. Drew Lock gets the start under center for the second time this season while veteran receiver Cooper Kupp could see a slight uptick in usage with Shaheed sidelined. Injury trouble along the offensive line could lead to a more ball-out-quick offensive game plan as the Seahawks look to keep pace in the NFC West.

Headline: Hunter Henry (foot) is active for Week 9 against the Packers.
News Snippet: It was reported earlier in the day that Henry had a “realistic” shot at suiting up this week after he managed to log a limited practice on Friday. Henry will profile as a high-end TE2 with A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) out this week. In addition to Brown being out, the Patriots also declared RB TreVeyon Henderson, CB Charles Woods, OT Dametrious Crownover, and QB Behren Morton inactive for Week 9.

Headline: Packers declared RB MarShawn Lloyd (knee), LB Zaire Franklin, OL Donovan Jennings, OL Sean Rhyan, OL Travis Glover, and TE Josh Whyle inactive for Week 9 against the Patriots.
News Snippet: Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson will serve as the backups to Josh Jacobs with Lloyd sidelined. DB Keisean Nixon, who was listed as questionable entering the weekend, is active after being slowed by a groin injury earlier in the week.

Headline: Cardinals declared RB Bam Knight, CB Starling Thomas V, LB Eku Leota, OL Jayden Williams, OL Jon Gaines III, and OL Albert Reese IV inactive for Week 9 against the Seahawks.
News Snippet: Knight’s absence due to a concussion leaves Tyler Allgeier alone atop the running back depth chart with rookie Jeremiyah Love on injured reserve. The matchup is far from ideal against the Seahawks on the road, but Allgeier appears to be in line for a legitimate workhorse role and can be started as a viable RB2. The Cardinals press forward with veteran journeyman Gardner Minshew under center following the trade of Jacoby Brissett this week.

Headline: Chargers did not activate David Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve for Week 9 against the Texans.
News Snippet: Njoku entered the contest listed as doubtful, although he practiced in a limited capacity all week. He might be able to return next week, but he does not need to be added in 12-team leagues. The Chargers declared LG Kayode Awosika (fibula), S Kendall Williamson (calf), CB Deane Leonard (concussion), WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) and WR Theo Wease inactive for Week 9 against the Texans.

Headline: Jaylen Waddle suffered a concussion in the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers and will not return.
News Snippet: Waddle was listed as questionable in the first half but then ruled out to begin the third. It’s another nightmare development for Waddle in his first Broncos season, as he has struggled for both 100 percent health and productive box scores. Today’s injury came as Waddle skied for a target over the middle of the field and got high/lowed. He had just one grab for 22 yards before departing. The only good news is the Broncos are on bye for Week 10, meaning Waddle might not miss any game time beyond this afternoon.

Headline: Texans declared David Montgomery, S Reed Blankenship, TE Cade Stover, OG Febechi Nwaiwu, OT Braden Smith and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 9 against the Chargers.
News Snippet: Montgomery will miss another week with his groin injury, allowing Woody Marks to qualify as a low-end, volume-based RB2. Montgomery did not practice at all this week. His status for the Texans’ Week 10 game against the Browns is up in the air. Fortunately for the Texans, S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) is making his return this week. Rookie TE Marlin Klein will also play.

Headline: Tyler Goodson (knee) is questionable to return to Week 9 against the Colts.
News Snippet: Goodson saw solid work early against the Colts, effectively rotating drives with starter Javonte Williams before injuring his knee in the second quarter. He was deemed questionable to return by the team after amassing 44 yards on seven carries. Expect Williams to operate as a workhorse for the remainder of the game.

Headline: Jake Ferguson (ankle) is ankle for Week 9 against the Colts.
News Snippet: Ferguson entered the weekend listed as questionable after being unable to practice until Friday, where he logged a limited appearance. That was apparently enough for the veteran tight end to play through the ailment, although Brevyn Spann-Ford could be more involved than normal.

Headline: Mike Gesicki caught 2-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 victory over the Falcons.
News Snippet: Gesicki had caught a touchdown in each of his last six games, but was essentially a non-factor in the win over the Falcons in Madrid. The Bengals scored three times in the red zone, but those touchdowns went to Tee Higgins (twice) and Joe Burrow. Gesicki needs those scores to be fantasy-relevant. He’ll be a touchdown-dependent TE2 heading into Week 10’s matchup with the Steelers.

Headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-2 targets for 16 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
News Snippet: The Falcons passing attack was a mess against the Bengals in Week 9. Michael Penix threw 31 times, but for just 162 yards. Dotson was a non-factor by product, totaling just 16 yards on two receptions. He’s Atlanta’s WR2, but is merely a WR5/6 heading into Week 10 against the Chiefs.

Headline: Kyle Pitts caught 3-of-5 targets for 23 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
News Snippet: Three receptions for 23 yards is a disappointing line and unfortunately it represents the most receiving yards Pitts has had in his last three games. Pitts has four touchdowns on the season, but is unusable in fantasy unless he finds the end zone. The definition of touchdown-dependent, Pitts is a low-end TE2 in Week 10 against the Chiefs.

Headline: Drake London caught 5-of-5 targets for 68 yards in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
News Snippet: London bounced back after being held to one reception and eight yards in the loss to the Buccaneers in Week 8. He caught all five of his targets for 68 yards, but still has only one touchdown on the year after being held scoreless again. After dominating with Michael Penix in the lineup last season, London has just been okay with Penix under center this year. Likely facing a pass-heavy game script in Week 10 against the Chiefs, London will be a low-end WR1 again.

Headline: Bijan Robinson rushed 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 9 loss to the Bengals, adding six receptions for 47 yards.
News Snippet: Robinson bounced back nicely after posting 76 scoreless yards in the loss to the Buccaneers in Week 8. The 24-year-old running back had 100 rushing yards and score while adding six catches for 47 yards through the air. Robinson’s touchdown gives him six in nine games this year after scoring 11 times in 17 games last season. Still an elite fantasy option despite the offense around him, Robinson is a locked in RB1 against the Chiefs in Week 10.

Headline: Michael Penix completed 20-of-31 passes for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Falcons’ 34-17, Week 9 loss to the Bengals.
News Snippet: Penix has now gone back-to-back weeks without eclipsing 200 yards. He found Charlie Woerner for a one-yard touchdown in the first quarter, but couldn’t get much going for the rest of the game. Wide receiver Drake London dominated in a small sample with Penix healthy last year, but he’s had just two games with at least 100 yards and only one touchdown this season. Penix is a low-end QB2 heading into Week 10’s home matchup against the Chiefs.

Headline: Samaje Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons.
News Snippet: Perine had 43 yards on 11 carries, which was notable because he had two more rushing attempts than starter Chase Brown. While Brown continues to underwhelm, Perine is cutting into Brown’s ceiling (or lack thereof) more than he’s carving out a legitimate role for himself. Perine is one of the better handcuffs to stash, but he shouldn’t be in starting lineups in Week 10 against the Steelers.

Headline: Chase Brown rushed nine times for 57 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three receptions for 18 yards.
News Snippet: While Brown struggled in Week 8, the silver lining was that he out-touched Samaje Perine 20-to-5. After fumbling against the Titans last week, Perine actually had more carries than Brown (11-to-9) in Madrid. Brown saw all three targets that went to running backs against the Falcons, but there’s no way to spin this positively for the 26-year-old who had a preseason ADP in the teens. Brown still hasn’t scored since Week 1 and he’ll be an RB2 at best against the Steelers in Week 10.

Headline: Chiefs declared CB Mansoor Delane, QB Garrett Nussmeier, FB Ben VanSumeren, DE Jack Pyburn, OT Diego Pounds, and DT Peter Woods inactive for Week 9 against the Jets.
News Snippet: The Kansas City defense will be without Delane against a Geno Smith-led Jets passing attack that showed out last week against the Raiders. The Chiefs this season are allowing the NFL’s 13th lowest EPA per drop back and rank 15th in drop back success rate allowed.

Headline: Trent McDuffie (back) is inactive for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
News Snippet: McDuffie was a DNP in practice all week but still managed to get a questionable designation entering the weekend. That said, the team’s decision doesn’t come as much of a surprise given the fact that he was unable to get on the field last week. Fortunately for the Rams, they faced a depleted Commanders receiving corps, and they will have both Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald on the field for the first time together.

Headline: Browns declared QB Deshaun Watson, QB Taylen Green, C Parker Brailsford, DT Maliek Collins, LB Justin Jefferson, and CB Noah Igninoghene inactive for Week 9 against the Saints.
News Snippet: Watson cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend but was not prepared as the starter throughout the week. Shedeur Sanders will get his first start of the season and Dillon Gabriel will back him up.

Headline: Colts declared TE Pharaoh Brown, LB Akeem Davis-Gaither, S AJ Haulcy, OT Charlie Heck, QB Riley Leonard, TE Will Mallory, and CB Justin Walley in active for Week 9 against the Cowboys.
News Snippet: No real surprises here as the Colts limp into their final game before the league’s trade deadline. That said there remains legitimate uncertainty surrounding the usages of Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs, amongst others, in what could be their final game with the franchise.

Headline: Broncos declared S Talanoa Hufanga, CB Kris Abrams-Draine, S Brandon Jones, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey, OG Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, and QB Sam Ehlinger inactive for Week 9 against the Panthers.
News Snippet: Hufanga was questionable entering the weekend due to an ankle injury, but will officially be sidelined for this one. The 28-year-old safety hasn’t played since Week 5 but was limited in back-to-back practices to close out the week, so there’s a chance he could return after the Broncos’ Week 10 bye.

Headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Eagles.
News Snippet: With Skattebo down, the G-Men have been forced into a Devin Singletary start. Someone named “Gregory Desrosiers” appears to be the RB2. Expect a pass-focused game plan vs. Philly’s crumbling defense. Also inactive for the Giants are CB Colton Hood, CB Nikko Reed, OL Josh Sills, OL Marcus Mbow, TE Thomas Fidone II and DL C.J. Okoye.

Headline: Panthers declared LB Jaelan Phillips, QB Haynes King, CB Will Lee III, RB AJ Dillon, LB Bobby Okereke, OG Damien Lewis, and DT TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 9 against the Broncos.
News Snippet: Phillips and Lewis were both ruled out before the weekend, so there’s nothing too surprising to see here. The Panthers hope to end a two-game losing streak this week at home against a stout Broncos defense.

Headline: Dolphins declared RB Jaylen Wright, WR Jalen Tolbert, TE Justin Joly, G Christian Haynes, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., and CB Reese Taylor inactive for Week 9 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Both Wright and Kaytron Allen were questionable because of quad injuries. Allen is active and will serve as Ollie Gordon’s backup.

Headline: Commanders declared WR Treylon Burks, QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, and OG Tanoa Togiai inactive for Week 9 against the Rams.
News Snippet: The Commanders find themselves incredibly thin at receiver with Burks (foot), Terry McLaurin (knee), and Dyami Brown (calf) all sidelined for this one. Stefon Diggs, along with rookie Antonio Williams could both be in line for busy days against a Rams secondary that will be without CB Trent McDuffie.

Headline: Jets declared Garrett Wilson, Tim Patrick, Nahshon Wright, Joseph Ossai, Trevin Wallace, Kohl Levao, and Blake Freeland inactive for Week 9 against the Chiefs.
News Snippet: Wilson suffered a head injury last week and did not practice this week as he remained in the NFL’s concussion protocol. Look for Omar Cooper, Jr. and Adonai Mitchell to see more routes and targets against a tough KC secondary. Mitchell is likely to function as the team’s top wideout with Wilson sidelined.

Headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
News Snippet: No surprises here as this was reported earlier today. St. Brown remains a top-flight WR1 for his matchup with the Phins. Sione Vaki is also active and will serve as the team’s RB2. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, EDGE DJ Wonnum, C Cade Mays, RB Jacob Saylors, TE Jordan Meeks, DL Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

Headline: George Pickens (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Colts.
News Snippet: Pickens played through the issue last week but will ultimately be held out in Week 9. Tight end Jake Ferguson is active after failing to practice until a limited showing Friday. Ryan Flournoy steps into a featured role for the Cowboys against the inside-funnel Colts defense. Fantasy managers can insert Flournoy into rosters as a viable FLEX considering he leads the team in slot rate through the first half of the season. Also inactive for the Cowboys are LB DeMarvion Overshown, WR KaVontae Turpin, CB Joey Porter Jr., LB Tyrus Wheat, OL Ajani Cornelius, and TE Luke Schoonmaker.

Headline: Vikings signed WR Odell Beckham from their practice squad to the active roster.
News Snippet: Beckham landed on the Vikings’ practice squad after being released by the Giants. He appeared in three games for New York and did not record any stats. Beckham hasn’t appeared in any games for Minnesota this year, but he’ll now be a member of their 53-man roster going forward.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that it “sounds like” the Jaguars are going to listen to trade offers for Brian Thomas Jr.
News Snippet: The Jags have shot down all offers so far, but it’s hard to justify his current usage when the team could instead recoup some draft capital by moving him. Thomas hasn’t caught more than two passes in a game since Week 2. He has three games with zero catches this year and played just 19 snaps on Thursday versus the Ravens. The Chiefs are reportedly interested, though that would require the Jags to send BTJ to one of their biggest competitors in the AFC. The Steelers and 49ers are also reportedly interested.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is “pushing to play” in Week 9 against the Eagles.
News Snippet: Skattebo was listed as doubtful for Week 9 after getting in a single limited practice this week. Players rarely suit up after getting the doubtful tag, but it’s not out of the question. Even if he is ruled out with inactives, the fact that Skattebo is pushing to play means he should be good to go for Week 10. Devin Singletary will handle the bulk of the backfield touches if he can’t go this week.

Headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Broncos are hopeful Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) will play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
News Snippet: Per Fowler, he remains a game-time decision. Hufanga logged two limited practices this week before receiving a questionable designation. Before going down with the injury, Hufanga had one forced fumble and two interceptions, one of which he took to the end zone. Getting him back would be a big win for the Denver defense.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Hunter Henry (foot) has a “realistic chance to play” in Week 9 against the Packers.
News Snippet: Henry only practiced once this week but still received a questionable designation on Friday. Eli Raridon would have taken his spot in the lineup, but it sounds like Henry will give it a go. He will be a high-end TE2 for his matchup with the Packers.

Headline: 49ers placed Christian Kirk (knee) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: Kirk missed the start of the year with a calf issue and immediately injured his knee in Week 7. The 49ers have already burned several injured reserve return designations this year, including one on Kirk himself. He could ultimately be stuck on IR for the remainder of the year, even if he’s not dealing with a catastrophic knee injury.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jaylen Wright (quad) will not play in Week 9 against the Lions.
News Snippet: Wright had been backing up Ollie Gordon before going down with the quad injury. Kaytron Allen is the next man up for RB2 duties, though he’s also dealing with a quad issue. Needless to say, we’re expecting a large workload for Gordon this week.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tanner McKee (rib) will serve as the Eagles’ backup quarterback in Week 9 against the Giants.
News Snippet: McKee was demoted to QB2 after Week 8. He suffered a rib injury in that game, but is healthy enough to hold a clipboard. Joe Milton will make his first career start versus the Giants today.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Sam Darnold (quad) could “potentially” miss Week 10 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: Garafolo added that Darnold is dealing with a cracked rib, though it sounds like the quad issue is what’s preventing him from playing. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald called Darnold “week to week” on Wednesday. They get their bye in Week 11, so holding him out for one more game to get an extended break makes the most sense. Fantasy managers should plan on Darnold missing Week 10 in addition to today’s game against Arizona. Drew Lock will start today. As long as his elbow issue doesn’t flare up, he will be in line to start next week as well.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes the Vikings are “a team to watch” for Daniel Jones.
News Snippet: Per Rapoport, the Ravens called Indy about Jones after Lamar Jackson went down with a potentially season-ending thumb injury. They eventually traded for Jacoby Brissett. With Kyler Murray hurt and playing poorly even when healthy, the Vikings are at least going to explore some outside options at quarterback. Jones was on the team’s practice squad in 2024 before joining the Colts last year.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports teams have “checked in on” Jadeveon Clowney.
News Snippet: Garafolo noted that the Texans’ game against the Chargers today will go a long way in determining whether the team wants to buy or sell at the trade deadline. Even at 2-5, the team thinks they can make a run at the playoffs. Clowney has been a hired-gun pass-rusher for most of his career. He isn’t starting for Houston and has just 1.5 sacks while playing a career-low 37 percent of the snaps on defense. If the Texans feel that their season is over, he will be one of the easiest players to move on from.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will have a “full workload” in Week 9 against the Raiders.
News Snippet: McCaffrey went down with the hamstring injury in Week 7, but then got a well-timed bye week to recover. He was a full participant in Friday’s practice before being removed from the injury report entirely. Per usual, he will be near the top of the RB1 ranks for his date with the Raiders.

Headline: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-6 targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 9 victory over the Falcons.
News Snippet: Higgins had recorded at least 148 receiving yards in three of his last four games. His 32 yards were a far cry from those gaudy totals, but he was able to save the day from a fantasy perspective by catching a four-yard touchdown and an eight-yard touchdown. Higgins still has 758 receiving yards on the season to Ja’Marr Chase’s 647, so he has that going for him. Higgins is technically the WR2 on the Bengals, but he’s a top-10 WR in fantasy heading into a matchup with the Steelers in Week 10.

Headline: Ja’Marr Chase caught 10-of-12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons.
News Snippet: Chase hadn’t had a game with 100 yards receiving until two weeks ago. Since then, he’s had at least 10 receptions, at least 141 yards and a touchdown in back-to-back games. Ho-hum. Chase absolutely toasted Falcons cornerback AJ Terrell for a 47-yard touchdown in the first quarter on a play that looked eerily similar to a touchdown he had against Terrell when the two were in college. Chase is up to 647 yards and seven touchdowns on the season. He’s a WR1 heading into Week 10’s matchup against the Steelers.

Headline: Joe Burrow completed 24-of-29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 34-17 Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three carries for seven yards and a touchdown.
News Snippet: Burrow’s excellent run of play continued against the Falcons defense in Madrid in Week 9. The 29-year-old signal caller has amassed 16 passing touchdowns in the last four weeks and added two more touchdowns on the ground. Burrow’s production is unsurprisingly coming from playing through his top wide receivers as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for 187 yards receiving and all three receiving touchdowns against Atlanta. Burrow is likely to find himself on the shortlist for the MVP award the way things are going. He’s a locked in QB1 heading into a Week 10 matchup with the Steelers on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

Headline: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is active for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
News Snippet: Parkinson managed to draw a questionable tag entering the weekend after logging a limited practice on Friday. Despite being a DNP for two of the Rams’ three practices this week, he should be available to play his normal role in the Rams’ TE-heavy scheme. Parkinson has caught 14 passes for 103 yards and one touchdown this season and will not be on the fantasy radar this week. The Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, LB Darryl Peterson III, OL Bill Murray, OL Keagan Trost, and LB Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 9.

Headline: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is active for Week 9 against the Browns.
News Snippet: Tyson will make his NFL debut after missing the first two months of the year with a hamstring injury. We’re expecting a snap count for him this week, making him an extremely risky FLEX play. Inactive for the Saints are QB Zach Wilson, S Mike Reid, RB C.J. Donaldson, DT Christen Miller, LB Jaylan Ford, OL Mason Murphy, and DL John Ridgeway III.

Headline: Eagles declared WR DeVonta Smith, WR Dontayvion Wicks, LB Jihaad Campbell, CB Jonathan Jones, S Michael Carter II and WR Britain Covey inactive for Week 9 against the Giants.
News Snippet: Smith has now been active just one time since Week 3. With the Eagles no longer particularly interested in the 2026 season, we would consider Smith no better than 50-50 to return following the team’s Week 10 bye.

Headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Mike Evans (Achilles) is “questionable at best” for Week 10 against the Cowboys.
News Snippet: The 49ers bungled Christian McCaffrey’s Achilles tendinitis in 2024 and are determined to get it right this time around with Evans. That means taking an extra cautious approach with his return to the field. He’s already been ruled out for Week 9 and now Week 10 sounds like a long-shot. Demarcus Robinson, who returned from injured reserve earlier this week, is somehow the team’s WR1 for today’s game against the Raiders.

Headline: NFL insider Josina Anderson reports the Giants “cooled on acquiring Colts RB Jonathan Taylor because of price.”
News Snippet: She added that the Giants have resolved to move on from the trade talks ahead of their Week 9 date with the Eagles. Things change quickly in the NFL and this report doesn’t guarantee that Taylor won’t be a Giant. On the other hand, Anderson’s reporting doesn’t leave much room error. With the Colts’ asking price reportedly being through the roof, the Giants are content with Cam Skattebo as their top back. Devin Singletary is expected to start this week with Skattebo banged up.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Deshaun Watson cleared the league’s concussion protocol but will be inactive for Week 9 against the Saints.
News Snippet: Watson returned to practice on Friday for a limited session and cleared the league’s protocol over the weekend. Still, after preparing Shedeur Sanders to start throughout the week, head coach Todd Monken decided not to throw a curveball at his own team on game day. Sanders will start and Dillon Gabriel will back him up. Watson has rebounded this year, but the lows are still staggeringly low. He took eight sacks in a blowout loss to the Steelers last week. If Sanders plays well today, Monken will at least have something to think about ahead of Week 10.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) will not play in Week 9 against the Bucs.
News Snippet: Per Rapoport, Monangai is expected to return after Chicago’s Week 10 bye. Monangai has been out since Week 4. He finally returned to practice earlier this week, but it was for a single, limited session on Friday. He should be back in a 1B role when the Bears take on the Saints in two weeks.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
News Snippet: St. Brown was limited in practice throughout the week. He has a knack for getting it out through injuries and will do so again today. Even at less than full strength, St. Brown shouldn’t face much resistance from Miami’s weak secondary. He remains a top-end WR1 for his Week 9 game in South Beach.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Emeka Egbuka (foot) will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
News Snippet: Egbuka missed two games with the foot injury, though a concussion also kept him out for one of them. He practiced in full on Friday, so we’re not expecting much of a pitch count for the second-year wideout. Without anyone emerging as a viable replacement for Egbuka over the past two weeks, he should reclaim the No. 1 receiver role in Tampa Bay without much of a fight. Egbuka will be on the WR2/3 border for his first game back.

Headline: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 9 against the Falcons.
News Snippet: The Bengals are surprisingly healthy headed into their date with the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. Dugger is the only one of their inactives who is out with an injury. The rest are healthy scratches.

Headline: Falcons EDGE James Pearce Jr. (back) is active for Week 9 against the Bengals.
News Snippet: Pearce Jr. just finished serving his eight-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. A back issue then flared up in practice, but he’s good to go for his 2026 debut. Inactive for the Falcons are QB Andy Dalton, QB Jack Strand, WR Zachariach Branch, DB Billy Bowman, DB Robert Longerbeam, and DE Drake Jackson.

Headline: Falcons placed RB Brian Robinson (hamstring) on injured reserve.
News Snippet: The timing of the transaction is curious after Robinson missed the previous two games with the injury, potentially signaling a setback in his recovery. Either way, Robinson will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, leaving Bijan Robinson in a clear workhorse role in the immediate future.

Headline: Broncos activated WR Pat Bryant (ankle) from injured reserve.
News Snippet: The young receiver will make his return to the active game-day roster after missing the minimum four games after injuring his ankle in Week 4. He returns to a passing attack with no clear direction or upside, with no receiver other than Courtland Sutton playing in a near every-down role of late. Perhaps he can carve out a featured role, but it is more likely this team simply doesn’t have viable weekly fantasy assets through the air.

Headline: 49ers activated WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) from injured reserve.
News Snippet: The veteran receiver returns to a decimated receiving corps, potentially in line to serve as the top receiver against the Raiders in Week 9. Fantasy managers in a bind could do much worse than taking a swing on Robinson considering the elite matchup and lack of viable depth, for a 49ers team with one of the week’s highest Vegas implied team totals on the board.

Headline: Vikings ruled out Jauan Jennings (calf) for Week 9 against the Bills.
News Snippet: The fantasy implications of Jennings’ absence are negligible, with the bigger boost to the passing offense being the absence of Kyler Murray, who is looking at a multi-game absence with a Grade 2 hamstring injury. Tai Felton appears to be in line for additional run as the team’s WR3, although he is not a recommended streaming option with both Jefferson and Jordan Addison healthy.

Headline: Vikings ruled out Kyler Murray (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Bills.
News Snippet: Murray will likely be sidelined for multiple games after testing revealed a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Carson Wentz will draw the start under center while the team is reportedly exploring the trade market ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. The absence of Murray should benefit alpha wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who has struggled to develop chemistry with Murray this season.

Headline: Dion Dawkins (ribs) and Alec Anderson (ankle) are questionable for Week 9 against the Vikings.
News Snippet: The Bills enter Week 9 with the entire left side of one the league’s top offensive lines questionable. Both players did not practice through Friday before drawing the questionable tag for Monday Night Football against the Vikings. We likely won’t know their respective statuses until inactives are released 90 minutes prior to first kick. Absences would be a detriment to the run game and could lead to increased emphasis on the short areas of the field through the air.

Headline: Bills ruled out Joshua Palmer (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Vikings.
News Snippet: Palmer has been in and out of the lineup since injuring his hamstring in Week 4, managing only seven offensive snaps last week before succumbing to an aggravation. He will miss his second game of the season when the Bills take on the one-loss Vikings on Monday Night Football. Skylar Bell could find himself active for the third time in his rookie season, although DJ Moore, Keon Coleman, and Khalil Shakir are likely to dominate snaps and routes at the position.

Headline: Saints released RB Kendre Miller.
News Snippet: The team brought back Audric Estime to their practice squad earlier in the week, releasing Miller Saturday. The moved comes after the veteran played 137 offensive snaps for a backfield missing its top option for most of the season. Miller had a 20-carry game for the Saints three short weeks ago and now finds himself without a home. Expect him to land on a practice squad in short order.

Headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
News Snippet: The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

Headline: Rams activated EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) from injured reserve.
News Snippet: No surprise here as Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Garrett is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders. The Rams are 4-4, but will finally have Garrett and Aaron Donald on the same defensive line. That could cause problems for opposing offensive lines, starting with Washington’s on Sunday.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Seahawks QB Drew Lock (elbow) has severe tendonitis in his elbow.
News Snippet: Pelissero reiterated that Lock looked good in practice and will start against the Cardinals in Week 9. Still, Lock has been dealing with this since earlier this season and at one point wasn’t able to throw because of it. Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald said earlier this week he didn’t know how much Lock will be able to throw. Despite his play in relief of Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) earlier this year, Lock isn’t a priority in 1QB leagues. Jalen Milroe could even be worth stashing in deeper formats given that Lock’s tendonitis could flare up at anytime.

Headline: NFL reporter Aaron Wilson reports RB Dameon Pierce (hamstring) is drawing interest from multiple teams.
News Snippet: Pierce was released by the Eagles after agreeing to an injury settlement on Friday. He’s currently still dealing with what Wilson described as a “relatively minor” hamstring injury. Wilson lists the Dolphins, Jaguars, Panthers, Ravens, 49ers, Cardinals and Titans as teams that have contracted Pierce, who is rehabbing in Houston. Expected to be ready in 2-3 weeks, Pierce could catch on with another team soon, though it’s unlikely to be in a starting role.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Titans WR Calvin Ridley “could be had for a late-round pick.”
News Snippet: The Titans are listening on Ridley, who could be had for a late-round pick, according to Schefter. The Chiefs, Steelers and 49ers are the most likely teams to be in the market for a wide receiver ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero also reported that multiple wide receivers could be traded before the deadline and listed Ridley as a name to watch.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Titans aren’t interested in trading RB Tony Pollard.
News Snippet: A previous report from Albert Breer suggested the team might be willing to trade Pollard, who is in the last year of his contract, for a fourth-round pick. Schefter threw cold water on that theory, reporting Tennessee isn’t interested in trading the 29-year-old running back. Showing fresh legs in recent weeks, Pollard is a solid RB2 the rest of the way even on a struggling Titans offense.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Commanders “haven’t completely abandoned” the idea of acquiring WR Brandon Aiyuk.
News Snippet: Aiyuk was rumored to end up in Washington all offseason and there seemingly could still be a fit there with Terry McLaurin out for the season. However, this report suggests the Commanders haven’t completely ruled it out rather than this being something they’re actively pursuing. Aiyuk met with 49ers brass Friday, though a resolution proved elusive. This saga is far from over.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have told teams they’ve received an offer of a fourth-round pick for WR Josh Downs.
News Snippet: The Colts’ original asking price for Downs, who has requested a trade, was a third-round pick. Indianapolis has told teams they already have an offer of a fourth-round pick for the 25-year-old receiver, who is in the last year of his rookie contract. Downs is probably one of the more likelier players to be traded ahead of the deadline. Teams have also called the Colts about Keenan Allen, though he’s unlikely to bring back a similar trade return given his age.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Chargers have no interest in trading EDGE Khalil Mack.
News Snippet: Despite the Chargers being 0-7, Los Angeles isn’t acting like it. Mack is 35, on an expiring contract and seeming could garner an early day-three pick in a trade. Still, the Chargers are content to keep Mack, who Schefter says won’t be going anywhere prior to the trade deadline.

Headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Broncos checked on Trey McBride.
News Snippet: To no one’s surprise, the Cardinals hung up the phone in record time. Even as a perennially rebuilding franchise, Arizona was never going to trade arguably the league’s best tight end in the middle of his prime. Schefter added that the Cardinals have “checked in around the league on tight ends.” Evan Engram has a measly 13 catches for 136 yards this year and Denver’s passing attack has taken a step back despite acquiring Jaylen Waddle in the offseason. Dallas Goedert is the biggest name believed to be available at tight end ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. On an expiring contract, he wouldn’t cost the Broncos much. Carolina tight end Ja’Tavion Sanders is likely on the trade block as well.

Headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Jets have no desire or intention to trade RB Breece Hall.
News Snippet: While the Jets traded young players for draft picks last season, don’t expect New York to do that again this year. A team source told Jones the Jets moving Hall is “very unlikely to happen.” Hall appears ready to return from a quad injury in Week 9 against the Chiefs, but is difficult to trust in fantasy with Braelon Allen potentially cutting into his workload after a strong showing in Hall’s absence in recent weeks.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Vikings QB Kyler Murray has a Grade 2 hamstring strain.
News Snippet: Previous reports said Murray was “week-to-week” with the injury. There’s no question the Vikings will monitor Murray’s health every week, but a Grade 2 hamstring strain typically leads to missing multiple games. With Carson Wentz set to start on Monday Night Football against the Bills in Week 9 and the Vikings monitoring outside QB options ahead of the trade deadline, Murray isn’t even guaranteed to be the starter again once he’s healthy.

Headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson is out for 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb.
News Snippet: Per Rapoport, Jackson has already told his teammates he plans to return this season. While even the short end of that timeline would only have Jackson back in Week 15, it’s an optimistic turn of events for a quarterback who was previously expected to miss the rest of the season. At a nine-week return, Jackson would need Baltimore to make the playoffs to have a shot at returning this year. Jacoby Brissett will likely close out the fantasy season as Baltimore’s starting quarterback, but there’s a chance we get Jackson back for a final game or two in the regular season.

Headline: Patriots activated WR Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve.
News Snippet: Hollins misses the minimum four games with a calf injury and returns to a pass catching corps without A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson, while tight end Hunter Henry is also listed as questionable for Week 9. There is opportunity for him to lead the team in receiving with the bulk of the remaining healthy players largely operating in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. Fantasy managers in a bid could do worse as a FLEX option against the Packers.

Headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts have told teams they aren’t trading QB Daniel Jones.
News Snippet: Despite ESPN’s Adam Schefter trying to will a Jones trade into existence by recreating Brian Windhorst memes, Pelissero reports the Colts have informed teams they aren’t trading the 29-year-old quarterback.
